akhfash:1-1.t: [He said] ﴿قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ ٱسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ﴾: the alif of ﴿أَنه﴾ has fatḥa because it is a noun. «[Translator's note: i.e., the clause stands in the position of a noun, the deputy agent of أُوحِيَ.]» Then He said ﴿وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا﴾ [3]: (with kasra) as a fresh beginning, since it is part of the speech of the jinn; and whoever reads it with fatḥa makes it dependent on "revelation" (الوحي), and that is good. «[Translator's note: the quotation of verse 3 is printed with fatḥa in the source, though the author is describing the reading with kasra, إِنَّهُ.]»

akhfash:8-8.t: And He said ﴿وَشُهُباً﴾; its singular is الشِّهاب (a shooting flame).

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿لِّنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ because you say "فَتَنْتُه" ("I tried him"), and some Arabs say "أَفْتُنُه"; so that (form) follows that dialect. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the dialectal form meant is presumably the Form IV أَفْتَنْتُه.]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ O Muhammad, to the people: ﴿أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ﴾ i.e. I have been informed by revelation from Allah the Exalted ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) ﴿اسْتَمَعَ﴾ to my recitation ﴿نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ the jinn of Naṣībīn; that was during the dawn prayer at Baṭn Nakhl, a place between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif; and they are the ones mentioned in His words, exalted is He: "And when We turned towards you a company of the jinn…" (the ayah). ﴿فَقَالُوا﴾ to their people when they returned to them: ﴿إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآنًا عَجَبًا﴾ one marvels at it for its eloquence, the abundance of its meanings, and other things;

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿يَهْدِي إِلَى الرُّشْدِ﴾ faith and what is right, ﴿فَآمَنَّا بِهِ وَلَنْ نُشْرِكَ﴾ after today ﴿بِرَبِّنَا أَحَدًا﴾

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), here and in the two places after it; ﴿تَعَالَى جَدُّ رَبِّنَا﴾ His majesty and greatness are far above what has been ascribed to Him; ﴿مَا اتَّخَذَ صَاحِبَةً﴾ a wife ﴿وَلَا وَلَدًا﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا﴾ our ignorant one ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ شَطَطًا﴾ excess in lying, by describing Him as having a wife and a child;

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا أَنْ﴾ lightened [from أَنَّ], i.e. أَنَّهُ ﴿لَنْ تَقُولَ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ by describing Him with that, until we saw clearly that they lied in that. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ رِجَالٌ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ يَعُوذُونَ﴾ seek refuge ﴿بِرِجَالٍ مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ when on their journeys they halt at a fearsome place, and each man says: "I seek refuge with the master of this place from the evil of its foolish ones." ﴿فَزَادُوهُمْ﴾ by their seeking refuge with them ﴿رَهَقًا﴾ arrogance, so they said: "We have become masters of the jinn and of mankind."

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ i.e. the jinn ﴿ظَنُّوا كَمَا ظَنَنْتُمْ﴾ O mankind ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened, i.e. أَنَّهُ ﴿لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ أَحَدًا﴾ after his death. The jinn said:

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا لَمَسْنَا السَّمَاءَ﴾ we sought to eavesdrop ﴿فَوَجَدْنَاهَا مُلِئَتْ حَرَسًا﴾ of angels ﴿شَدِيدًا وَشُهُبًا﴾ burning stars; and that was when the Prophet ﷺ was sent.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا كُنَّا﴾ i.e. before his being sent ﴿نَقْعُدُ مِنْهَا مَقَاعِدَ لِلسَّمْعِ﴾ i.e. we would listen; ﴿فَمَنْ يَسْتَمِعِ الْآنَ يَجِدْ لَهُ شِهَابًا رَصَدًا﴾ i.e. lying in wait for him, to be shot at him.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا لَا نَدْرِي أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ﴾ by the ending of eavesdropping ﴿بِمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ أَرَادَ بِهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ رَشَدًا﴾ good.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا مِنَّا الصَّالِحُونَ﴾ after hearing the Quran ﴿وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. people who are not righteous; ﴿كُنَّا طَرَائِقَ قِدَدًا﴾ differing groups, Muslims and unbelievers.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا أَنْ﴾ lightened, i.e. أَنَّهُ ﴿لَنْ نُعْجِزَ اللَّهَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَنْ نُعْجِزَهُ هَرَبًا﴾ i.e. we cannot escape Him, whether being on the earth or fleeing from it into the heaven.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعْنَا الْهُدَى﴾ the Quran ﴿آمَنَّا بِهِ فَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِرَبِّهِ فَلَا يَخَافُ﴾ with هُوَ implied (muqaddar) after the fāʾ ﴿بَخْسًا﴾ a reduction of his good deeds ﴿وَلَا رَهَقًا﴾ wrong by an increase in his bad deeds.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا مِنَّا الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا الْقَاسِطُونَ﴾ those who deviate by their unbelief; ﴿فَمَنْ أَسْلَمَ فَأُولَئِكَ تَحَرَّوْا رَشَدًا﴾ they aimed at guidance;

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا الْقَاسِطُونَ فَكَانُوا لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبًا﴾ fuel. وَأَنَّا, وَأَنَّهُمْ and وَأَنَّهُ in twelve places — namely وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَى and وَأَنَّا مِنَّا الْمُسْلِمُونَ and what lies between them — are read with kasra on the hamza, as resumptive, and with fatḥa on it, by whatever way it can be justified. Allah the Exalted said concerning the unbelievers of Mecca:

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَأَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy [أَنَّ], its noun omitted, i.e. وَأَنَّهُمْ, and it is conjoined to أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ: ﴿لَوِ اسْتَقَامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ i.e. the way of Islam, ﴿لَأَسْقَيْنَاهُمْ مَاءً غَدَقًا﴾ abundant, from the sky; and that was after rain had been withheld from them for seven years,

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ﴾ to test them ﴿فِيهِ﴾ so that We know how their gratitude is, with a knowledge of manifestation. ﴿وَمَنْ يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾ the Quran, ﴿نَسْلُكْهُ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ [يَسْلُكْهُ], We will make him enter ﴿عَذَابًا صَعَدًا﴾ arduous.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ﴾ the places of prayer ﴿لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدْعُوا﴾ in them ﴿مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَدًا﴾ by associating partners, as the Jews and Christians, when they entered their synagogues and churches, associated partners.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ with fatḥa, and with kasra as resumptive; the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); ﴿لَمَّا قَامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ﴾ Muhammad the Prophet ﷺ ﴿يَدْعُوهُ﴾ worshipping Him at Baṭn Nakhl, ﴿كَادُوا﴾ i.e. the jinn listening to his recitation ﴿يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَدًا﴾ with kasra on the lām and with ḍamma, plural of لِبْدَة, like felt (al-libd) in their mounting one upon another, crowding out of eagerness to hear the Quran.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ answering the unbelievers in their saying "Give up what you are engaged in" — in one reading [قُلْ] — ﴿إِنَّمَا أَدْعُوا رَبِّي﴾ as God ﴿وَلَا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ أَحَدًا﴾

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنِّي لَا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا﴾ error ﴿وَلَا رَشَدًا﴾ good.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنِّي لَنْ يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ from His punishment if I disobey Him ﴿أَحَدٌ وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿مُلْتَحَدًا﴾ a refuge,

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿إِلَّا بَلَاغًا﴾ an exception from the object (mafʿūl) of أَمْلِكُ, i.e. I have no power [to do anything] for you except conveying to you ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. from Him ﴿وَرِسَالَاتِهِ﴾ conjoined to بَلَاغًا; what lies between the thing excepted from (al-mustathnā minhu) and the exception is a parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ) to emphasise the denial of ability. ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ in [the matter of] the divine unity, and so does not believe, ﴿فَإِنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of مَنْ in لَهُ, out of regard for its meaning; it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), and the meaning is: they enter it, their remaining forever being decreed, ﴿فِيهَا أَبَدًا﴾

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا رَأَوْا﴾ [حَتَّى is] inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), carrying the sense of a limit to something implied before it, i.e. they will remain in their unbelief until they see ﴿مَا يُوعَدُونَ﴾ of the punishment, ﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾ when it befalls them on the day of Badr or on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿مَنْ أَضْعَفُ نَاصِرًا وَأَقَلُّ عَدَدًا﴾ in helpers: they or the believers, on the first view; or I or they, on the second. Then one of them said: "When is this promise?", and there was revealed:

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنْ﴾ i.e. مَا ﴿أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ مَا تُوعَدُونَ﴾ of the punishment ﴿أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ رَبِّي أَمَدًا﴾ a limit and a term that none but He knows.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ﴾ what is hidden from the servants; ﴿فَلَا يُظْهِرُ﴾ He does not disclose ﴿عَلَى غَيْبِهِ أَحَدًا﴾ of the people,

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضَى مِنْ رَسُولٍ فَإِنَّهُ﴾ along with disclosing to him whatever of it He wills, as a miracle for him, ﴿يَسْلُكُ﴾ He places and sends ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ﴾ i.e. of the messenger ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَدًا﴾ angels who guard him until he conveys it among the rest of the revelation,

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿لِيَعْلَمَ﴾ Allah, with a knowledge of manifestation, ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy, i.e. أَنَّهُ ﴿قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا﴾ i.e. the messengers ﴿رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — by making the pronoun plural, regard was given to the meaning of مَنْ — ﴿وَأَحَاطَ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ conjoined to something implied, i.e. so He knew that ﴿وَأَحْصَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَدًا﴾ a tamyīz (specification), converted from the object; the underlying form is: He counted the number of every thing.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿أُوحِيَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ﴾ anna and its noun, and a past verb. ﴿نَفَرٌ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of نفر; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from anna, its noun and its predicate is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of أوحي; the clause «أوحي..» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَقالُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause استمع. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿سَمِعْنا قُرْآناً﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عَجَباً﴾ an adjective; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿إِلَى الرُّشْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is a second adjective (ṣifa) of قرآنا. ﴿فَآمَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَلَنْ نُشْرِكَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِرَبِّنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is also conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and anna and its noun. ﴿تَعالى جَدُّ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), i.e. He is exalted above what is ascribed to Him. ﴿رَبِّنا﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿مَا اتَّخَذَ﴾ mā is negative, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿صاحِبَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا وَلَداً﴾ conjoined to صاحبة; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ كانَ﴾ anna and its noun, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir). ﴿يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنا﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the clause of kāna is the khabar of anna, and the clause أنه is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يقول. ﴿شَطَطاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ لَنْ تَقُولَ﴾ an is lightened (mukhaffafa), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan. ﴿الْإِنْسُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَالْجِنُّ﴾ conjoined to الإنس. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كَذِباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause لن تقول is the khabar of the lightened an, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from the lightened an, its noun and its predicate stands in place of the two objects of ظننا.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ كانَ رِجالٌ﴾ anna and its noun, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الْإِنْسِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of رجال. ﴿يَعُوذُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the clause of kāna is the khabar of أنه, and the clause أنه is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿بِرِجالٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يعوذون. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ an adjective of رجال. ﴿فَزادُوهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَهَقاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّوا﴾ anna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أنهم, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿كَما﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿ظَنَنْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿أَنْ﴾ an, lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿أَحَداً﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar of an, and the maṣdar formed from the lightened an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of ظن.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لَمَسْنَا السَّماءَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَوَجَدْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مُلِئَتْ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿حَرَساً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿شَدِيداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of حرسا. ﴿وَشُهُباً﴾ conjoined to حرسا; the clause ملئت is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا كُنَّا﴾ anna and its noun, and kāna and its noun. ﴿نَقْعُدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كنا, and the clause كنا is the khabar of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مَقاعِدَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿لِلسَّمْعِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb نقعد. ﴿فَمَنْ يَسْتَمِعِ﴾ man is a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿الْآنَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿يَجِدْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿شِهاباً﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَصَداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of شهابا; the clause يجد is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause of من is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لا نَدْرِي﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿أَشَرٌّ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation. ﴿شَرٌّ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb. ﴿أُرِيدَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِمَنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause أريد is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position, and the clause أشر stands in place of the two objects of ندري. ﴿أَمْ أَرادَ﴾ a conjunction and a past verb. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿رَبُّهُمْ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿رَشَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿مِنَّا﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿الصَّالِحُونَ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the khabar of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَمِنَّا﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿دُونَ﴾ an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a postponed mubtadaʾ, according to Ibn Hishām in al-Shudhūr. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿طَرائِقَ﴾ its khabar. ﴿قِدَداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of طرائق; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ﴾ an, lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَنْ نُعْجِزَ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the Name of Majesty is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar of the lightened an. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the interpreted maṣdar formed from the lightened an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of ظننا. ﴿وَلَنْ نُعْجِزَهُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿هَرَباً﴾ ḥāl.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive. ﴿سَمِعْنَا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْهُدى﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and لما with what it governs is the khabar (predicate) of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿من﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُؤْمِنْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِرَبِّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa). ﴿لا يَخافُ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause of من is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بَخْساً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿رَهَقاً﴾ conjoined to بخسا; its meaning is: injustice.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَأَنَّا﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿مِنَّا﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿الْمُسْلِمُونَ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the khabar of أنا, and the clause أنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَمِنَّا الْقاسِطُونَ﴾ conjoined to its like; القاسطون means: those who deviate unjustly through their disbelief. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿من﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَسْلَمَ﴾ a past verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَأُولئِكَ تَحَرَّوْا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and a demonstrative as mubtadaʾ, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar of أولئك. ﴿رَشَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause أولئك is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause of من is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:15-15.t: [Translator's note: the quotation marks and the beginnings of the Quranic words are corrupted in the source here («َ أَمَّا» … «مَّا» … «لْقاسِطُونَ» … «َكانُوا» … «ِجَهَنَّمَ» … «َ طَباً»); the words are restored below from the verse وَأَمَّا الْقاسِطُونَ فَكانُوا لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَباً.] «وَأَمَّا» the wāw is a resumptive particle. «أمّا» a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl). «الْقاسِطُونَ» mubtadaʾ (subject). «فَكانُوا» the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and kāna and its noun. «لِجَهَنَّمَ» a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial). «حَطَباً» khabar (predicate) of كانوا; the clause كانوا is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause «أما القاسطون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ﴾ an, lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). ﴿لَوِ﴾ conditional, not making jussive. ﴿اسْتَقامُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ﴾ the lām occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ماءً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿غَدَقاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ماء; its meaning is: abundant. The clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of an, and the clause of an is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb أسقيناهم. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُعْرِضْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm). ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يعرض. ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَسْلُكْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَذاباً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿صَعَداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of عذابا; the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من, and the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ﴾ anna and its noun; and ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of anna; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: the verb تدعوا is not quoted in the source]; and ﴿مَعَ اللَّهِ﴾ an adverb of place annexed to the Name of Majesty; and ﴿أَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿لَمَّا قامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ﴾ لما is a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿يَدْعُوهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿كادُوا﴾ كاد and its noun. ﴿يَكُونُونَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its noun. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿لِبَداً﴾ khabar; the clause يكونون is the khabar of كاد, and the clause كادوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and لما with what it governs is the khabar of أنه, and the clause «أنه..» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّما﴾ a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿أَدْعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿رَبِّي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا أُشْرِكُ﴾ negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أدعو.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun; and ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿أَمْلِكُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿ضَرًّا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿رَشَداً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ضرا; the clause «لا أملك..» is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَنْ يُجِيرَنِي﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, and the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the first person is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾ fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلَنْ أَجِدَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the accusative by lan, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مُلْتَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿بَلاغاً﴾ excepted (mustathnā), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) بلاغا. ﴿وَرِسالاتِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بلاغا. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿مِنَ﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the word in the verse is مَن]. ﴿يَعْصِ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined to the Name of Majesty. ﴿فَإِنَّ﴾ the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of the condition, and a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿نارَ﴾ the postponed noun of inna. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدين. ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time; the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause «من..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of beginning (ḥarf ibtidāʾ); and ﴿إِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive. ﴿رَأَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the sīn of futurity, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿أَضْعَفُ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi, and the clause «سيعلمون..» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿ناصِراً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿وَأَقَلُّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أضعف. ﴿عَدَداً﴾ tamyīz.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative. ﴿أَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَقَرِيبٌ﴾ the hamza of interrogation; and ﴿قَرِيبٌ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of أدري, and the clause «إن أدري..» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); and ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَجْعَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); and ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿رَبِّي﴾ fāʿil; and ﴿أَمَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿عالِمُ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause «هو عالم» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُظْهِرُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عَلى غَيْبِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿أَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿مَنِ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ارْتَضى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مِنْ رَسُولٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَإِنَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and inna and its noun. ﴿يَسْلُكُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes them. ﴿رَصَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar of من.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿لِيَعْلَمَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb يسلك; and ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); and ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿أَبْلَغُوا رِسالاتِ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the lightened an, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from the lightened an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يعلم. ﴿وَأَحاطَ﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial), and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ an adverb of place; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَأَحْصى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أحاط; and ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, annexed to ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَدَداً﴾ tamyīz (specification).

dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَفَرٌ) al-nafar: a group of between three and ten. In al-Qāmūs: «al-nafar is all the people, and fewer than ten men, like al-nafīr; the plural is anfār». In the commentary on al-Qāmūs: «Abū al-ʿAbbās said: al-nafar, al-rahṭ and al-qawm — these have the meaning of a plural and have no singular from their own form; the relative adjective from it is nafarī. Al-Zajjāj said: al-nafīr is the plural of nafar, like al-ʿabīd».
(جَدُّ رَبِّنا) His greatness, from your saying جدّ فلان في عيني, i.e. he became great [in my eyes]. In the ḥadīth of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "When a man among us read al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān, he became great (jadda) among us". More of its discussion will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَقالُوا إِنَّا سَمِعْنا قُرْآناً عَجَباً) قل is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta", i.e. O Muhammad. أوحي is a past passive verb and إليّ is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أوحي; anna and what falls in its scope is in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). Anna and its noun, and the clause استمع is its khabar (predicate); نفر is the agent of استمع and من الجن is an adjective of نفر. فقالوا is conjoined to استمع; inna and its noun, and the clause سمعنا is the khabar of إنا; قرآنا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and عجبا an adjective (naʿt), i.e. one marvels at it because of its eloquence and rhetorical excellence, the sublime meanings it contains, and other things. (يَهْدِي إِلَى الرُّشْدِ فَآمَنَّا بِهِ وَلَنْ نُشْرِكَ بِرَبِّنا أَحَداً) The clause يهدي إلى الرشد is a second adjective of قرآنا, and إلى الرشد is attached to يهدي. فآمنا is conjoined to سمعنا and به is attached to آمنا. ولن: the wāw is a conjunction and lan is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; نشرك is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan; بربنا is attached to نشرك, and أحدا is the direct object of نشرك. (وَأَنَّهُ تَعالى جَدُّ رَبِّنا مَا اتَّخَذَ صاحِبَةً وَلا وَلَداً) The wāw is a conjunction, and anna and what falls in its scope is conjoined to what preceded. Anna and its noun; تعالى is a past verb and جد ربنا its agent, and the clause is parenthetical between the noun and the khabar; the clause ما اتخذ is the khabar of anna; ولا ولدا is conjoined to صاحبة. (وَأَنَّهُ كانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنا عَلَى اللَّهِ شَطَطاً) conjoined to what preceded. Anna and its noun, and the clause كان is its khabar; the noun of kāna is latent, its implied form being "huwa"; سفيهنا is the agent; على الله is attached to يقول; شططا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. a شطط saying, i.e. going to extremes in lying, and that by describing Him as having a consort and a child. The clause يقول is the khabar of kāna. [Translator's note: the source gives both a latent noun of kāna and سفيهنا as agent of يقول, as written.] (وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا أَنْ لَنْ تَقُولَ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً) وأنّا is conjoined to what preceded; anna and its noun, and the clause ظننا is its khabar. ظنّ is a past verb, one of the verbs of the heart, and نا is the agent; an is lightened [from anna] and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause لن تقول is its khabar. Lan is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; الإنس is the agent and الجن is conjoined to الإنس; على الله is attached to تقول; كذبا is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar. (وَأَنَّهُ كانَ رِجالٌ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجالٍ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَزادُوهُمْ رَهَقاً) وأنه is also conjoined; anna and its noun, and the clause كان is its khabar; رجال is the noun of kāna and من الإنس an adjective of رجال; the clause يعوذون is the khabar of kāna; برجال is attached to يعوذون and من الجن is an adjective of رجال. فزادوهم is conjoined to كان رجال; زادوهم is a verb, its agent and its first direct object, and رهقا is the second object. (وَأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّوا كَما ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنْ لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ أَحَداً) وأنهم is also conjoined to what preceded; anna and its noun, and the clause ظنوا is its khabar. كما is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; the clause ظننتم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative [mā]. An and what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of ظنوا; an is lightened from the heavy [anna], its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter; lan is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; يبعث is an imperfect verb in the accusative by lan, and the clause is the khabar of an; الله is the agent of يبعث and أحدا its object. (وَأَنَّا لَمَسْنَا السَّماءَ فَوَجَدْناها مُلِئَتْ حَرَساً شَدِيداً وَشُهُباً) also conjoined to what preceded. Anna and its noun, and the clause لمسنا is its khabar; السماء is the direct object — the meaning of touching the sky will come under rhetoric. The fāʾ is a conjunction; وجدناها is a verb, its agent and its direct object, and the clause ملئت is the second direct object. ملئت is a past passive verb, the tāʾ being the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and the deputy agent is latent, its implied form being "hiya", i.e. the sky. حرسا is a tamyīz (specification) and شديدا an adjective; شهبا is conjoined to حرسا. It is also said that وجدناها here takes one object, so the clause ملئت is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because its meaning is "we came upon it". (وَأَنَّا كُنَّا نَقْعُدُ مِنْها مَقاعِدَ لِلسَّمْعِ فَمَنْ يَسْتَمِعِ الْآنَ يَجِدْ لَهُ شِهاباً رَصَداً) also conjoined to what preceded. Anna and its noun, and the clause كنا is its khabar; kāna and its noun, and the clause نقعد is the khabar of كنا; منها is attached to مقاعد; مقاعد is an adverb of place attached to نقعد; للسمع is attached to an implied element that is an adjective of مقاعد, i.e. seats that are for listening. The fāʾ is a conjunction; من is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ (subject); يستمع is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); الآن is an adverb of the present, borrowed for the future, attached to يستمع; يجد is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); له is in the place of the second object of يجد; شهابا is the first object of يجد and رصدا an adjective of شهابا; it has the meaning of a passive participle, i.e. made ready and prepared for him.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words, the Exalted, «تعالى جدّ ربنا» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), because it is borrowed from fortune (al-ḥaẓẓ), which is luck and prosperity, since the rich are those who are fortunate (majdūdūn). The meaning is describing Him as exalted above having a consort and a child, because of His greatness and His self-sufficiency.
2- In His words «وأنّا لمسنا السماء» there is a synecdoche-type metaphor (majāz mursal), because al-mass is touching (al-lams), and the toucher is one who seeks to find out. A poet said:
مسسنا من الآباء شيئا وكلنا ... إلى نسب في قومه غير واضع
(We have attained something from the fathers, and each of us belongs to a lineage among his people that is not low.)
The verse is by Yazīd ibn al-Ḥākim al-Kilābī. مسسنا means "we attained", so the touching is a majāz mursal. Each of us belongs to a lineage among his people that is not lowly — it is also transmitted "to a noble standing (ḥasab)" — so we were equal with respect to the fathers in boasting; but when we reached the mention of the mothers in it, you found your relatives "generous of bedding" — a metonymy for wives, or the name of the place is used for what is in it, namely the wives, as a majāz mursal. Women's generosity is blameworthy because it is a metonymy for indecency, just as their stinginess is used as a metonymy for chastity; so we are not equal with respect to the mothers. After it comes:
فلما بلغنا الأمهات وجدتم ... بني عمكم كانوا كرام المضاجع
(But when we came to the mothers, you found that your cousins were "generous of bedding".)

dervis-irab:10-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قِدَداً) plural of qidda, with kasra, which is the way. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «al-qidda is the way and a faction of people; the plural is qidad, like sidra and sidar. Some say: a faction of people when each one's inclination is separate». It is gathered from al-Lisān and others that one says كنا طرائق قددا, i.e. factions with differing inclinations. It is also given the plural aqidda.
(الْقاسِطُونَ) those who deviate unjustly through their disbelief. Al-qāsiṭ is the one who deviates unjustly, because he has turned away from the truth, and al-muqsiṭ is the one who is just, turning to the truth; from qasaṭa when he deviated unjustly, while the four-letter aqsaṭa means "he was just". It is reported from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that al-Ḥajjāj said to him, when he wanted to kill him: "What do you say about me?" He said: "Qāsiṭ, ʿādil". The people said: "How well he spoke!", thinking that he was describing him with equity (qisṭ) and justice (ʿadl). Al-Ḥajjāj said: "O ignorant ones, he has called me a wrongdoer and an associator", and he recited to them the words of the Exalted: «وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا» and «ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون».
(تَحَرَّوْا رَشَداً) i.e. they aimed at guidance and sought it diligently. From it is al-taḥarrī in a thing; one says حرى الشيء يحريه, i.e. he aimed at its ḥarā, i.e. its side, and تحرّاه likewise. So said al-Rāghib, but what is in the lexicons is that حرى الشيء means "it decreased".
(غَدَقاً) al-ghadaq, with fatḥa or kasra on the dāl, two dialectal forms, for abundant water; from it is al-ghaydāq for much water, and for a man who runs a lot and who talks a lot. In al-Miṣbāḥ:
«غدقت العين غدقا, of the pattern of تعب: its water became abundant, so it is غدقة. In the Revelation:
لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا, i.e. abundant. أغدقت إغداقا likewise. غدق المطر غدقا and أغدق إغداقا are similar. غدقت الأرض تغدق, of the pattern of ضرب, when it became soaked with abundant water».
(صَعَداً) with fatḥa on the ṣād and the ʿayn, the maṣdar (verbal noun) of صعِد, with kasra on the ʿayn, like فرِح.
(لِبَداً) with kasra on the lām, and it was read with fatḥa on it; they are two dialectal forms. It is the plural of libda, with kasra on the lām, like sidra and sidar, on the [first] form, and on the second form like ghurfa and ghuraf. In al-Mukhtār: «al-libd, on the pattern of al-jild, is the singular of al-lubūd, and al-libda is more specific than it. I say: its plural is libad, and from it are His words, the Exalted: كادوا يكونون عليه لبدا». The wording of al-Qurṭubī:
«Mujāhid said: لبدا, i.e. groups. It is from a thing's تلبّد upon a thing, i.e. gathering together; from it is al-libd (felt) which is spread out, because its wool is heaped up. Anything you have stuck firmly you have labbadtahu. The hair on the back of a lion is called libda, its plural being libad. Much locust is called libad. There are four dialectal forms in it, and they are readings: with fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra on the lām, which is the reading of the majority; with ḍamma on the lām and fatḥa on the bāʾ, which is the reading of Mujāhid, Ibn Muḥayṣin and Hishām of the people of Syria, its singular being lubda, with ḍamma on the lām, or with kasra; with ḍamma on the lām and the bāʾ, which is the reading of Abū Ḥayyān [Translator's note: so in the source; probably Abū Ḥaywa is meant], Abū al-Ashhab, al-ʿUqaylī and al-Jaḥdarī, its singular being labd, like suquf from saqf and ruhun from rahn; and with ḍamma on the lām and a doubled bāʾ with fatḥa, which is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū al-ʿĀliya and also al-Jaḥdarī, its singular being lābid, like rākiʿ and rukkaʿ, and sājid and sujjad».

* I'rab:
(وَأَنَّا لا نَدْرِي أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ أَرادَ بِهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ رَشَداً) وأنا is conjoined to what preceded; anna and its noun, and the clause لا ندري is its khabar (predicate). In أشرّ there are two views: the nominative by an implied verb on the basis of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), and second, the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause أريد being the khabar. The first is preferable, because of the precedence of what calls for a verb, namely the interrogative hamza. بمن is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أريد, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of أريد is latent (mustatir); on the first view the clause أريد is explicative and has no grammatical position. في الأرض is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. Am is a conjunction of equivalence (muʿādila); بهم is attached to أراد, ربهم is the fāʿil (agent) and رشدا the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). More discussion of this verse will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَأَنَّا مِنَّا الصَّالِحُونَ وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذلِكَ) also conjoined. منا is a fronted khabar and الصالحون a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of أنا. منا is a fronted khabar, and دون is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is the delayed mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: and of us is a party or a group below that. Al-Akhfash and others permitted دون to have the meaning of غير, i.e. and of us are other than the righteous, and it is the mubtadaʾ; it was given fatḥa only because it is in construct with a non-declinable word, as in His words لقد تقطع بينكم in the reading of those who read it in the accusative, according to one of the views. The first is preferable. Omission of the qualified noun with partitive min is common, as in their saying منا ظعن ومنا أقام, i.e. of us a party departed and of us a party stayed. ذلك is muḍāf ilayhi. (كُنَّا طَرائِقَ قِدَداً) In it there are several views. First, that the implied form is: we were possessors of ways, i.e. of different doctrines. Second, that the implied form is: we were, in the difference of our states, like different ways. Third, that the implied form is: we were in different ways. Fourth, that the implied form is: our ways were qidad (divided), on the omission of the muḍāf, which is الطرائق, and putting the pronoun that was muḍāf ilayhi in its place. In any case, kāna and its noun, طرائق is its khabar and قددا an adjective (naʿt). On the third view طرائق is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the preposition and its genitive noun is the khabar of كنا. Abū Ḥayyān was not pleased with this view and said: «As for the third implied form, namely that it is accusative on the dropping of في, that is not permissible except in poetic necessity. Sībawayh stated explicitly that عسل الطريق is anomalous, so the Qur'an is not to be construed on it». By عسل الطريق Abū Ḥayyān meant the saying of Sāʿida ibn Juʾayya describing a spear:
لدن بهز الكف يعسل متنه ... فيه كما عسل الطريق الثعلب
(Supple, its shaft quivering when the palm shakes it, as the fox trots along the road.)
The point of evidence in it is his words عسل الطريق, where he omitted the preposition and put in the accusative the noun that had been genitive by it; the original form of the speech is عسل في الطريق, and it is a poetic necessity. (وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا أَنْ لَنْ نُعْجِزَ اللَّهَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَنْ نُعْجِزَهُ هَرَباً) also conjoined. ظننا is a verb and its agent; an is lightened from the heavy [anna], and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause لن نعجز الله is its khabar; an and what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of ظننا. في الأرض is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ولن نعجزه is conjoined to لن نعجز الله; هربا is a maṣdar in place of a ḥāl, its implied form being: we shall not escape Him while being on earth wherever we move about in it, and we shall not escape Him fleeing to the sky and going far into it. (وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعْنَا الْهُدى آمَنَّا بِهِ) also conjoined. Anna and its noun; لما is connective or temporal; سمعنا is a verb and its agent and الهدى the direct object; the clause آمنا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition that does not cause the jussive; به is attached to آمنا. (فَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِرَبِّهِ فَلا يَخافُ بَخْساً وَلا رَهَقاً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; من is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ; يؤمن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its agent is "huwa"; بربه is attached to يؤمن. The fāʾ is connective; lā is negative and يخاف is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), its agent being "huwa"; the clause لا يخاف is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then he does not fear", and the nominal clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis. بخسا is the direct object and ولا رهقا is conjoined to بخسا. The reason for the verb's being nominative and for implying a mubtadaʾ before it so that it serves as its khabar will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَأَنَّا مِنَّا الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا الْقاسِطُونَ) also conjoined to what preceded. Anna and its noun; منا is a fronted khabar and المسلمون a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of أنا; ومنا القاسطون is conjoined to منا المسلمون. (فَمَنْ أَسْلَمَ فَأُولئِكَ تَحَرَّوْا رَشَداً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; من is a conditional noun causing the jussive, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; أسلم is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ is connective; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and the clause تحروا is the khabar; رشدا is the direct object. (وَأَمَّا الْقاسِطُونَ فَكانُوا لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَباً)
The wāw is a conjunction; أما is a particle of condition and detailing; القاسطون is a mubtadaʾ; the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive; كانوا is a defective past verb and the wāw is its noun, and the clause is the khabar of القاسطون; لجهنم is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of حطبا and was put first; حطبا is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause is the khabar of القاسطون. (وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ ماءً غَدَقاً) also conjoined, to أنه استمع. An is lightened from the heavy [anna], and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter, i.e. and it has been revealed to me that if they had kept straight. Law is conditional, and the clause استقاموا is the khabar of an [Translator's note: so in the source; normally the whole conditional sentence is taken as the khabar]; على الطريقة is attached to استقاموا. The lām occurs in the apodosis of law; أسقيناهم is a verb, its agent and its first direct object; ماء is the second direct object, and عذقا [Translator's note: so in the source, a misprint for غدقا] is an adjective of ماء. (لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ وَمَنْ يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ عَذاباً صَعَداً) The lām is the lām of cause; نفتنهم is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the causal lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to أسقيناهم; فيه is attached to نفتنهم. The meaning is: so that We may test them in the water and know, with a knowledge that becomes manifest to creation, how they give thanks and how they are ungrateful; otherwise He, glory be to Him, is all-knowing and nothing is hidden from Him. The wāw is a conjunction; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; يعرض is the protasis; عن ذكر ربه is attached to يعرض; يسلكه is the apodosis and the hāʾ is the direct object, i.e. He makes him enter. عذابا is accusative by removal of the preposition, the original being نسلكه في عذاب, as in His words, the Exalted: واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا. صعدا is an adjective; صعدا is the maṣdar of صعِد, with kasra on the ʿayn, like فرِح, and the punishment is described by it by interpreting it as an active participle, i.e. a rising punishment that overwhelms him, rises above him and sweeps him away. (وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً) conjoined to أنه استمع, i.e. it has been revealed to me that the places of prostration belong to Allah, i.e. are exclusive to Him. Anna and its noun, and لله is its khabar. The fāʾ is a conjunction; lā is prohibitive and تدعوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; مع الله is an adverb attached to تدعوا, and أحدا is the object of تدعوا. (وَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا قامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يَدْعُوهُ كادُوا يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً) also conjoined to أنه استمع. Anna and its noun; لما is connective, or a temporal adverb containing the meaning of condition; قام عبد الله is a past verb and its agent; the clause يدعوه is a ḥāl, i.e. calling upon Him. What is meant by him is Muhammad ﷺ, i.e. performing the dawn prayer, or simply worship, at Baṭn Nakhla. The clause كادوا has no grammatical position because it is
the apodosis of لما; and its condition and its apodosis are the khabar of أنه. Kāda is one of the verbs of approximation, the wāw is its noun and the clause يكونون is its khabar; the wāw in يكونون is the noun of يكون; عليه is attached to an omitted ḥāl, and لبدا is the khabar of يكونون.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «وأنّا لا ندري أشر أريد بمن في الأرض أم أراد بهم ربهم رشدا» there is a difference in the form of speech because of the difference of situations. The form of speech before am differs from the form after it, because the first has the verb of willing in the passive and the second has the verb of willing in the active. The situation calling for that is attributing good to Him, glory be to Him, in the second, and refraining from attributing evil to Him in the first. Ibn al-Munayyir said: «Among their beliefs — i.e. the jinn's — is that guidance and misguidance are both willed by Allah the Exalted, by their saying وأنا لا ندري (the verse). They showed fine courtesy in mentioning the willing of evil with the agent omitted, while the one willing is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in bringing out His name when [mentioning] the willing of good and guidance; so they combined sound belief and graceful courtesy». The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «When they saw what had happened — the abundance of pelting and the prevention of eavesdropping — they said: وأنا لا ندري أشر أريد بمن في الأرض أم أراد بهم ربهم رشدا, so that they would believe in Him and be rightly guided. When they mentioned evil, they did not ascribe it to Allah the Exalted, and when they mentioned guidance, they ascribed it to Him, the Exalted».
2- In His words «وأنّا لما سمعنا الهدى آمنا به فمن يؤمن بربه فلا يخاف بخسا ولا رهقا» there is the device of clarification (al-īḍāḥ). The discussion of it has preceded, and that it is the resolving of a difficulty arising from the outward form of the speech; it occurs in the meanings of badīʿ in words and in their i'rab, and in the meanings of the soul apart from the other devices; we mentioned it in detail in Āl ʿImrān. The apparent [construction] is certainly dispensing with the fāʾ and putting the verb in the jussive, avoiding the implying of a mubtadaʾ before it; but He turned away from what is apparent for a benefit, namely that when He did that, it is as though it were said "then he does not fear", so it indicated the certainty that the believer is saved without doubt and that he alone, and no one else, is singled out for that. From another angle, the nominal clause is more indicative and more emphatic than the verbal clause in affirming the content of the clause.

dervis-irab:20-28.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُلْتَحَداً): al-multaḥad: the place of refuge; it is said: a way of escape; and it is said: a place to turn aside to. The wording of al-Qāmūs: «ألحد إليه: he inclined [to it], like التحد; al-multaḥad is the refuge (al-multajaʾ)». In al-Miṣbāḥ:
«al-multaḥad, with fatḥa, is the noun of place, and it is the refuge».
(وَأَحْصى) The origin of iḥṣāʾ is that when the one counting reached a certain decade among the decades of numbers, such as ten, a hundred and a thousand, he would put down a pebble (ḥaṣāt) to keep by it the quantity of that decade, and then build his counting upon it.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ إِنَّما أَدْعُوا رَبِّي وَلا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ أَحَداً) a resumptive statement, set out to reply to the disbelievers who were banding together against him, saying to him: "You have undertaken a grave matter that it never occurred to anyone else to undertake; so go easy on yourself and turn away from it, and we will protect you". قال [Translator's note: so in the source, although the verse as quoted reads قل; قال is the reading of other readers, and the remark below that "it was read قل" reflects the same reversal] is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring to the Prophet, upon him be peace. إنما is the restraining [mā] with what it restrains (kāffa wa-makfūfa). أدعو ربي is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The wāw is a conjunction, lā is negative, and أشرك is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "anā"; به is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أشرك, and أحدا is the direct object. It was read قل, by way of a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to address. (قُلْ إِنِّي لا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا رَشَداً) also a resumptive statement, set out to reply to them and to make clear his inability [to control] his own affairs and that the whole matter is in the hand of Allah. Inna and its noun, and the clause لا أملك is its khabar (predicate); لكم is attached to ضرا; ضرا is the direct object, and ولا رشدا is conjoined to ضرا. The clause إني لا أملك is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (قُلْ إِنِّي لَنْ يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ أَحَدٌ وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداً) Inna and its noun, and the clause لن يجيرني is the khabar; من الله is attached to يجيرني and أحد is the agent of يجيرني. ولن أجد is conjoined to لن يجيرني; من دونه is in the place of the second object of يجدني [Translator's note: so in the source, for أجد], and ملتحدا is the first object. (إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِسالاتِهِ) إلا is a particle of exception. Concerning بلاغا there are several views:
1- That it is an exception from the object of أملك, i.e. from the combination of the two things, ضرا and رشدا, after interpreting them as "anything", as though he said: I possess nothing for you except conveying; so it is a connected exception. On this view there are two views on its being accusative:
the first, that it is a badal (substitute) from ملتحدا, because the speech is not affirmative; the second, the accusative as an excepted noun.
2- That it is a disconnected exception, because conveying from Allah does not fall under His words ولن أجد من دونه ملتحدا, and because it is not "apart from Allah" but rather from Allah and with His help.
3- That it is an exception from His words لا أملك لكم ضرا. Al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied form, saying: «i.e. I possess nothing except conveying from Allah; and قل إني لن يجيرني is a parenthetical clause, inserted to emphasise the negation of ability from himself and to make clear his helplessness, in the sense that if Allah wanted harm for him — illness, death or other — no one could rightly protect him from it, nor could he find, apart from Him, a refuge to resort to». Abū Ḥayyān judged this view far-fetched. What follows is the text of his wording, because of its excellence: «إلا بلاغا: al-Ḥasan said it is a disconnected exception, i.e. no one will protect me, but if I convey, my [Lord's] mercy [will protect me] by that [Translator's note: the source reads «إن بلغت رحمتي بذلك», which seems garbled]. Protection is attributed to conveying metaphorically, since it is the cause of Allah's protection and mercy. It is said that on this meaning it is a connected exception, i.e. no one will protect me, but I have found nothing to incline to and hold fast to except that I convey and obey, and then Allah will protect me; so it may be accusative as an exception from ملتحدا, or as a badal, which is the [better] view because what precedes it is a negation; al-Zajjāj explained it as a badal. Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī said: This exception is disconnected, because He did not say "and I will not find a refuge", but rather said "apart from Him", and conveying from Allah does not fall under His words من دونه ملتحدا, because it is not apart from Allah, but rather from Allah and by His help and enabling. Qatāda said: the implied form is: I possess nothing except conveying to you; as for faith and disbelief, I do not possess them. End [of quote]. This is far-fetched because of the long separation between them. It is also said that إلا is to be taken as separated [into two parts]: in is conditional and lā negative, and its verb is omitted because the maṣdar indicates it, the implied form being: if I do not convey a conveying from Allah and His message. This is as you say: إن لا قياما قعودا, i.e. if you do not stand a standing, then sit a sitting. The omission of this verb may be because what is after it or before it indicates it, as it was omitted in the saying:
فطلقها فلست لها بكفء ... وإلا يعل مفرقك الحسام
(So divorce her, for you are no match for her; and if not, the sword will rise above the parting of your hair.)
The implied form is: and if you do not divorce her; تطلقها was omitted because فطلقها indicates it. Min is for the beginning of the extent». Abū al-Baqāʾ confined himself to the disconnected exception, because it is not of the same genus. من الله is an adjective (naʿt) of بلاغا, and رسالاته is conjoined to بلاغا; al-Zamakhsharī chose this and said: «It is as though it were said: I possess nothing for you except the conveying and the message; and the meaning is: except that I convey from Allah, saying "Allah said such-and-such", attributing His words to Him, and that I convey His messages with which He sent me without addition or diminution». Abū Ḥayyān, al-Samīn and al-Karkhī preferred that it be conjoined to الله, i.e. except from Allah and from His messages. Both are sound. (وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً) The wāw is resumptive; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); يعص is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its agent is latent, its implied form being "huwa"; the Name of Majesty is the direct object and رسوله is conjoined to it. The fāʾ connects the apodosis; inna is a particle resembling the verb, له is its fronted khabar and نار جهنم its delayed noun; خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in له, and what governs this ḥāl is the omitted [notion of] being settled. خالدين is plural by construing it according to the plural meaning in من. فيها is attached to خالدين, and أبدا is an adverb of time, also attached to خالدين. (حَتَّى إِذا رَأَوْا ما يُوعَدُونَ فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَضْعَفُ ناصِراً وَأَقَلُّ عَدَداً) حتى here is an inceptive particle, i.e. a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar may come after it, and despite that it has the meaning of limit. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: To what is حتى attached, with what follows it made a limit for it? I say: To His words يكونون عليه لبدا, on the basis that they band together against him in enmity, deem his supporters weak and consider their number small, until, when they see what they are promised — the day of Badr and Allah's giving him the upper hand over them, or the Day of Resurrection — they will know then that they are the weaker in helpers and fewer in number. It may also be attached to an omitted element indicated by the situation — the disbelievers' deeming him weak and considering his number small — as though He said: they will continue in what they are in until, when they see what they are promised … The associators said: "When will this promised thing be?", denying it; so it was said: Say: it is certainly coming, there is no doubt about it, so do not deny it, for Allah has promised that and He does not break the promise; as for its time, I do not know when it will be, because Allah has not made it clear, on account of the benefit He saw in concealing its time». إذا is an adverb for future time, putting its condition in the genitive, accusative by its apodosis; the clause رأوا is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it. رأوا is a past verb and its agent; ما is a relative noun, the direct object; the clause يوعدون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The fāʾ connects the apodosis; the sīn is a particle of the future; يعلمون is an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition that does not cause the jussive. Here there is a difficulty that none of those who undertook the interpretation and i'rab of this verse has pointed out: the sīn is a particle of the future, while the knowledge of who is weak and who is strong comes about immediately at the time of seeing the punishment, whereas the sīn requires that it come later than it. There is no escape from this difficulty except by making the sīn a particle of mere emphasis, not of the future. Furthermore, حتى إذا may be attached to an omitted element indicated by the situation — the disbelievers' deeming him weak and considering his number small — as though He said: they will continue in what they are in until, when they see what they are promised … The associators said: "When will this promised thing be?", denying it; so it was said to them: it was said that it is certainly coming, there is no doubt about it, so do not deny it, for Allah has promised that and He does not break the promise; as for its time, I do not know when it will be. The wording of al-Jalāl: «حتى إذا رأوا is inceptive, with the meaning of a limit for something implied before it, i.e. they will remain in their disbelief until they see what they are promised of punishment; then they will know when it befalls them». من may be interrogative, so it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and أضعف is its khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يعلمون, because it suspends the verb of knowing before it. It may also be a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a direct object, with أضعف the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "he is weaker", and the clause is the ṣila; on this view, knowing has the meaning of recognising, so it does not need two objects. ناصرا is a tamyīz (specification), and أقل عددا is conjoined to أضعف ناصرا. Moreover, Abū Ḥayyān raised an objection to this i'rab that we have given; we quote it verbatim. He said, in the course of his reply to al-Zamakhsharī:
«His saying "To what is it attached?": if he meant the attachment of a preposition, it is not correct, because it is an inceptive particle, so what is after it is not in the position of the genitive — contrary to al-Zajjāj and Ibn Durustawayh, who claimed that when it is an inceptive particle, the inceptive clause after it is in the position of the genitive. If by attachment he meant the connection of what is after it with what is before it, and what is after it being a limit for what is before it, then it is correct. As for his estimation that it is attached to His words يكونون عليه لبدا, that is very far-fetched because of the long separation between them by many clauses. Al-Tibrīzī said: حتى may be a limit for something omitted, but he did not make clear what the omitted thing is. It is said: the meaning is: leave them until, when they see what they are promised of the Hour, they will know who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number, they or the People of the Book? What appears to me is that it is a limit for what the preceding clause contains, namely the judgement that the Fire is theirs, as though it were said: the disobedient one is judged to have the Fire as theirs, and the judgement of that is a threat, until, when they see what was judged to be theirs, they will know. So His words فإن له نار جهنم are a threat to them with the Fire. من أضعف is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative by what precedes it, which is suspended from governing it because من is interrogative. It may also be a relative noun in the position of the accusative by سيعلمون, with أضعف the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the clause being the ṣila of من, its implied form being "he is weaker"; its omission is made acceptable by the lengthening of the ṣila by the governed word, namely ناصرا». (قُلْ إِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ ما تُوعَدُونَ أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ رَبِّي أَمَداً) قل is an imperative verb and its agent is latent, its implied form being "anta"; in is negative; أدري is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) and its agent is latent, its implied form being "anā". The hamza is interrogative; قريب is a fronted khabar and ما توعدون a delayed mubtadaʾ. قريب may also be a mubtadaʾ because it relies on the interrogative, with ما توعدون as its agent, i.e. is that which you are promised near?, as in أقائم أبواك. ما may be a relative noun, so the returning pronoun is omitted and the clause توعدون is the ṣila; or it may be maṣdariyya, so there is no returning pronoun. Am is connected (muttaṣila); يجعل is an imperfect verb in the nominative; له is in the place of the second object; ربي is the agent and أمدا is the first object of يجعل. The clause suspended by the interrogative is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of أدري. (عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ فَلا يُظْهِرُ عَلى غَيْبِهِ أَحَداً) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the Knower"; it may also be parsed as a badal from ربي. The fāʾ is a conjunction, to make the not disclosing follow upon His being uniquely the Knower of the unseen absolutely. Lā is negative and يظهر is an imperfect verb in the nominative; على غيبه is attached to يظهر, and أحدا is the direct object. (إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضى مِنْ رَسُولٍ فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً) إلا is a particle of restriction and the exception is disconnected, i.e. but whomever He has approved, He discloses to him what He wills of His unseen through revelation. من is a relative or conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ in either case; on the conditional view the clause فإنه is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The exception may also be connected, i.e. except a messenger whom He has approved, so من is parsed as a badal from أحد. من بين يديه is attached to يسلك; ومن خلفه is conjoined to من بين يديه; رصدا is the object of يسلك, and the clause يسلك is the khabar of إنه, i.e. He sends angels as watchers. (لِيَعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا رِسالاتِ رَبِّهِمْ) The lām is the lām of cause; يعلم is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the causal lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to يسلك as a purpose for it, inasmuch as it follows upon the conveying which follows upon it. Al-Qurṭubī attached it to an omitted element; his wording: «In it there is an omission to which the lām is attached, i.e. We informed him of Our preserving the revelation so that he may know that the messengers before him conveyed the message just as he conveyed the message». [Translator's note: the quotation is not closed in the source; it is assumed to end here.] An is lightened from the heavy [anna], and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); qad is a particle of realisation, and the clause أبلغوا رسالات ربهم is the khabar of an. (وَأَحاطَ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ وَأَحْصى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَداً) conjoined to something implied, i.e. so He knew that. أحاط is a past verb and its agent is latent, its implied form being "huwa", referring to Allah the Exalted; بما is attached to أحاط; لديهم is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila. أحصى is conjoined to أحاط; كل شيء is the object of أحصى; عددا is a tamyīz converted from the object, i.e. He has counted the number of everything. Al-Zamakhsharī parsed it as a ḥāl; his wording:
«عددا is a ḥāl, i.e. He has registered everything as counted and enumerated; or it is a maṣdar with the meaning of iḥṣāʾ (counting)». Abū al-Baqāʾ began with the maṣdar view and permitted the tamyīz. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān:
«عددا, i.e. counted; it is accusative as a ḥāl from كل شيء, even though it is indefinite, because the definite is included in the generality. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar of أحصى, because it is in the meaning of iḥṣāʾ».

* Benefits:
A dispute arose between Ahl al-Sunna and the Muʿtazila about the miracles (karāmāt) of the saints. Al-Zamakhsharī said, in discussing His words, the Exalted, «عالم الغيب فلا يظهر على غيبه أحدا», after a long discussion: «In this is the invalidation of karāmāt, because those to whom they are attributed, even if they are approved saints, are not messengers, and Allah has singled out the messengers, from among those approved, for acquaintance with the unseen. [In it is also] the invalidation of soothsaying and astrology, because their practitioners are the farthest of things from being approved and the most deeply sunk in [Allah's] displeasure».
Ibn al-Munayyir followed him up, saying: «He claimed something general and adduced evidence for something particular. His claim is the invalidation of karāmāt in all their kinds, while what the verse indicates is the invalidation of the saint's acquaintance with the unseen specifically; and a karāma or a breach of the customary is not only acquaintance with the unseen. The Qadariyya always have some specious argument for invalidating them, and that is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, never takes a saint from among them, and they have never been told of that about their partisans; so no wonder they persist in denial, not knowing that the condition of a karāma is sainthood, which is by agreement withheld from them — as for the withholding of faith, that is a disputed question … He wants the karāma because he has not been given it».
Al-Qurṭubī took another direction and said: «The scholars said: Since He, glory be to Him, praised Himself for knowledge of the unseen and reserved it to Himself to the exclusion of His creation, there is in that an indication that no one knows the unseen besides Him. Then He excepted those He approved from among the messengers, and entrusted to them what He willed of His unseen by way of revelation to them, and made it a miracle for them and a true indication of their prophethood». Then he mentioned an argument for the falsity of what the astrologer says, and then he held that the astrologer's blood may lawfully be shed.
Al-Wāḥidī said: «In this is evidence that whoever claims that the stars indicate what will happen of life, death or other things has disbelieved in what is in the Qur'an».
Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī said: «Al-Wāḥidī permits karāmāt, according to what the author of al-Kashshāf said, by making [the verse] indicate the prohibition of astrological judgements, while it does not indicate [anything about] inspirations — a mere specious resemblance. [Translator's note: this sentence is garbled in the source and is rendered as closely as possible.] In my view the verse indicates nothing of what they said, because His words على غيبه have no form of generality in them», until he says: «Know that it must be decided that what is meant by this verse is not that no one becomes acquainted with anything of the unseen except the messengers, upon them be blessing and peace. What indicates this are several considerations. First: it is established by reports close to mass-transmission that Shiqq and Saṭīḥ were two soothsayers who foretold the appearance of Muhammad ﷺ before the time of his appearance, and they were famous among the Arabs for this kind of knowledge, so much so that Chosroes referred to them to learn about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Second: the agreement of the nations on the soundness of the science of dream interpretation; the interpreter informs about what will come in the future and is truthful.
Third: the Baghdadi soothsayer woman whom Sultan Sanjar ibn Malikshāh moved from Baghdad to Khurāsān; he asked her about things in the future and she told of them, and they happened in accordance with her words. I have seen people who are expert in the sciences of kalām and philosophy who reported of her that she told of hidden things in detail and they turned out so. Abū al-Barakāt, the author of al-Muʿtabar, went to great lengths in describing her state in the book of dream interpretation and said: I investigated her state for thirty years until I became certain that she used to tell of hidden things with accurate, matching reports.
Fourth: we observe people of true inspirations, and this is not restricted to the saints; for in sorcerers and in astrological reports there is found what agrees with the truth, even if lying occurs from them frequently. If that is observed and perceptible, then saying that the Qur'an indicates the opposite of it leads to attacking the Qur'an, and that is false; so we know that the correct interpretation is what we have mentioned».
Abū Ḥayyān followed him up and said: «We have only cited this man's words on this question in order to examine the considerations he mentioned. As for the story of Shiqq and Saṭīḥ, there is nothing in it of informing about the unseen, because it is what the soothsayers' familiar spirits from among the devils, who eavesdrop, tell them, as has come in the ḥadīth that they hear a word [Translator's note: the source has «وبل الكلمة», apparently a misprint] and lie, and pass it on to the soothsayers, and the soothsayers add a hundred lies to the word. This is not knowledge of the unseen, since the angels spoke it, the jinn snatched it, and the soothsayer snatched it from him; so the soothsayer did not know the unseen. As for the interpretation of dreams, the interpreter, who is not infallible, does not interpret with certainty and decisiveness, but by way of estimation and conjecture; what he interprets may happen and may not happen. As for the Baghdadi soothsayer woman and what is reported of her, it is enough [to judge] his intelligence that he adduces as evidence the states of a woman he did not witness; and had he witnessed that, there would have been in his intelligence what would allow that it was not as described — and he is the learned author whose fame has filled the horizons, and the one who cast doubt on the proofs of the philosophers and subjected them to humiliation. As for what he reports from the author of al-Muʿtabar, he was a Jew who professed Islam and adopted the method of the philosophers. As for his observing people of true inspirations, I am about seventy-three years old, I have kept the company of scholars and frequented those who claim righteousness, and I have not seen any of them who had true inspiration. As for karāmāt, I do not doubt that some of them occur, but that is rare, and it was among the righteous of this community in the past; perhaps in our times there may be someone from whom a karāma issues, and Allah the Exalted may single out whomever He wills with whatever He wills».

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أُوحِىَ إِلَىَّ﴾.
The readers are agreed [218/a] on (أُوحِىَ). Juwayya al-Asadī read it: "قُلْ أُحِىَ إِلَىَّ", from وحيتُ, putting a hamza for the wāw because it took a ḍamma, as He said: ﴿وإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ﴾.
His saying: ﴿ٱسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِّنَ ٱلْجِنِّ﴾.
It is mentioned that when the devils were pelted and the sky was guarded against them, Iblīs said: This is a prophet who has appeared. So he spread his troops through the horizons, and sent nine of them from Yemen to Mecca. They came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was at Baṭn Nakhla, standing in prayer and reciting the Qurʾān. It pleased them, their hearts softened towards it, and they became Muslim; and of their words is what Allah has related in this sura.
