The readers are agreed on kasra in "إِنا" in His saying: ﴿فَقَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآناً عَجَباً﴾, but they differed on what comes after that: they read وإنّا and وأَنَّا to the end of the sura, giving kasra to some and fatḥa to some.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh, the brother of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, and Qays told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama ibn Qays, that he read what is in [Sūrat] al-Jinn and al-Najm: (وأنا) with fatḥa. Al-Farrāʾ said: and Yaḥyā, Ibrāhīm and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh used to read it so. Nāfiʿ al-Madanī read with fatḥa, while al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and most of the people of Medina read with kasra, except that they read with fatḥa: ﴿وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ للهِ﴾ (18). [Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: After the account of the jinn was related, there was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿وَأنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلهِ فَلاَ تَدْعُواْ﴾ (18).
ʿĀṣim used to read with kasra what was part of the jinn's speech, and with fatḥa what was part of the revelation. As for those who read all of them with fatḥa, they joined "أنَّ" back each time to His saying: فآمنا به — "and we believed in all of that" — so أن received fatḥa because "believing" acts upon it. Yet with that you find "believing" fits well in some of what has fatḥa and is awkward in others; but that does not prevent you from carrying them all through with fatḥa, for where an overt "we believed" is awkward, a verb akin to "believing" may fit well and require the fatḥa of أنَّ, as the Arabs said:
إذا ما الغانيات بَرَزْنَ يوماً * وزَجّجن الحَواجبَ والعُيونا
(When the fair women come out one day, having thinned their eyebrows and [darkened] their eyes.)
He put العيون in the accusative by making it follow الحواجب, although eyes are not thinned but only darkened with kohl; so he implied "kohl" for them. Likewise, in a place where آمنَّا (we believed) does not fit, one implies [a verb] that does fit: صدقنا (we affirmed), ألهمنا (we were inspired), شهدنا (we bore witness). The accusative reading is strengthened by His saying: ﴿وَأَنْ لَّوِ اسْتَقَامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ﴾ (16).
So whoever reads with kasra ought to drop (أنْ) from (لو), because (أنْ), when lightened, does not occur in quoted speech; do you not see that you say: أقول لو فعلتَ لفعلتُ (I say: had you done it, I would have done it), without introducing (أنْ)?
As for those who read all of them with kasra, they say in that case: ﴿وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقَامُوا﴾ as though they implied an oath with لو and cut it off from the sequence joined to the beginning of the discourse, saying: والله أن لو استقاموا (by Allah, if they had kept straight). The Arabs put أن in this position with an oath, and also drop it. The poet said:
فأقسمُ لو شىء أتانا رسُوله * سواك، ولكن لم نجدْ لكَ مدفَعا
(I swear, had anything other than you sent us its messenger [we would have repelled it]; but we found no way to repel you.)
And another recited to me:
أمَا واللهِ أنْ لو كُنتَ حُرًّا * وما بِالحرِّ أنتَ ولا العتيقِ
(By Allah, if you were a free man — but you are neither free-born nor freed.)
Whoever reads all of them with kasra but reads ﴿وأن المساجد لله﴾ with fatḥa has singled it out as revelation, and has treated وأنْ لو as containing an implied oath, as I have described to you.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنَّا لاَ نَدْرِيۤ أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
This is from the speech of the unbelievers among the jinn; they said: We do not know whether this was done because good is intended for them or because of evil — meaning the pelting of the devils with the stars.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُنَّا طَرَآئِقَ قِدَداً﴾.
We were different sects, our inclinations differing. الطريقة is a man's way. It is also said [109/a] of a group: they are the طريقة of their people, when they are their leaders; and of one person too: [he is] the طريقة of his people. Likewise it is said of one person: this is the نظورة of his people, of the one whom they look up to; some of the Arabs say: نظيرة of his people; and both are pluralised نظائر.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن نُّعْجِزَ ٱللَّهَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
[I.e.] we knew with certainty.
One of the readers read: "أن لن تَقوَّل الإنسُ والجنُّ", but I will not name him.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ يَخَافُ بَخْساً ﴾: nothing will be diminished from the reward of his deed, ﴿وَلاَ رَهَقاً﴾.
Nor wrong.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَّا ٱلْقَاسِطُونَ﴾: they are the unjust, the unbelievers; and المقسطون are the just, the Muslims. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَنْ أَسْلَمَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ تَحَرَّوْاْ رَشَداً﴾.
He is saying: they made for guidance and followed it.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَلَّوِ ٱسْتَقَامُواْ عَلَى ٱلطَّرِيقَةِ﴾: on the way of unbelief, ﴿لأَسْقَيْنَاهُم مَّآءً غَدَقاً﴾ — it would be an increase in their wealth and their livestock. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿ولَوْلاَ أَنْ يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِّن فِضَّةٍ﴾. He is saying: that is done to them so that it may be a trial for them in this world and an increase in the punishment of the Hereafter.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُعْرِضْ عَن ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ عَذَاباً صَعَداً﴾.
It came down concerning al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī. They mention that الصَّعَد is a smooth rock in Hell which he is made to climb; when he reaches its top, he is thrown down into Hell, and that is his constant lot. Similar to it in Sūrat al-Muddaththir: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً﴾.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱلْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلاَ تَدْعُواْ﴾.
So do not associate with Him in them any idol or anything that is worshipped. It is said: [it means] these mosques. And it is said: وأن المساجد لله means a man's places of prostration: what he prostrates on — his forehead, his hands, his knees and the fronts of his feet.
[Translator's note: «يسحد» is as printed, for «يسجد».]

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا قَامَ عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ يَدْعُوهُ﴾.
He means the Prophet ﷺ, on the night the jinn came to him at Baṭn Nakhla. ﴿كَادُواْ يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً﴾: they almost climbed on top of the Prophet ﷺ out of longing for the Qurʾān and desire for it.
Some read: "لُبُدا", and the meaning of both — and Allah knows best — is one; one says لُبدَة and لِبدة.
Whoever reads "لُبَّداً" means to make it an adjective of men, as in your saying: رُكّعاً and ركوعا, سجَّدا and سجودا.

farraa:20-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَدْعُو رَبِّي﴾. Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read: "قُلْ إنما أدعُو ربِّى", and the generality of the people of Medina read likewise; some [read] (قال), and some (قل).
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] Muḥammad told us, he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl told me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may Allah have mercy on him — that he read it: (قال إنما أَدْعُو رَبِّى).
The readers are agreed on ﴿لاَ أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرّاً﴾ with fatḥa on the ḍād; none of them read it with ḍamma.

farraa:22-22.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداً﴾: a refuge, or a burrow in which I could take refuge.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ بَلاَغاً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِسَالاَتِهِ﴾.
It may be an exception from His saying: "I have no power to cause you harm or right guidance, except that I convey to you what I have been sent with".
There is another way in it: Say: none will protect me from Allah if I do not convey His message. Then the accusative of البلاغ is by an implied verb belonging to the conditional (jazāʾ), as you say to a man: إِلا قياماً فقعودا (if not standing, then sitting) and إلا عطاء فردا جميلا (if not a gift, then a gracious refusal), i.e. if you do not do [it], then [let it be] at least a gracious refusal. So لا is separate from إن [i.e. إلا = إنْ لا]. This is a good way. The Arabs say: إِن لا مال اليوم فلا مال أبدا (if there is no wealth today, there will be no wealth ever), treating (لا) as the lā of generic negation (tabriʾa); they also use the nominative with that meaning; and whoever uses the accusative with tanwīn does so by an implied verb. One of the Arabs recited to me:
فإن لا مَال أعطيه فإنى * صديق من غُدو أو رَواح
(If there is no wealth for me to give, then I am a friend, morning or evening.)

farraa:27-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنِ ٱرْتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولٍ﴾.
For He acquaints him with [110/a] His unseen.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَسْلُكُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً﴾.
They mention that when Jibrīl ﷺ came down with the message to the Prophet ﷺ, angels from every heaven came down with him, guarding him against the jinn listening to the revelation in order to steal it and cast it to their soothsayers, so that they would anticipate the Prophet ﷺ with it. That is the guard before him and behind him. Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لِّيَعْلَمَ﴾, meaning Muḥammad ﷺ, ﴿أَن قَدْ أَبْلَغُواْ رِسَالاَتِ رَبِّهِمْ ﴾, meaning Jibrīl ﷺ. Some said: it is Muḥammad ﷺ, i.e.: Muḥammad knows that he has conveyed the message of his Lord.
Some read: "لِيُعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا", meaning: so that the jinn and mankind may know that the messengers have conveyed [the message], [and] not they [the jinn], with what they hoped for from eavesdropping.
[Translator's note: «لاهم» is as printed; it is read here as «لا هم» ("not they").]

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] Muḥammad told us, he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Abū Isrāʾīl told me, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا﴾; he said: the majesty of our Lord.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾.
ظن here means doubt.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَن يَسْتَمِعِ ٱلآنَ﴾: since Muḥammad ﷺ was sent, he finds for himself a meteor lying in wait, set in ambush for him to pelt him.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أنه استمع» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the hāʾ in «أنه» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). The preposition and its genitive noun «من الجن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نفر», and the clause «فقالوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «استمع».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «يهدي» is a second naʿt (adjective) of {قُرْآنًا}; the clause «فآمنَّا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {سَمِعْنَا}; and the clause «ولن نشرك» is conjoined to the clause «آمنَّا».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «ما اتخذ» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; the clause «تعالى جَدُّ» is parenthetical; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made of «أن» and what follows it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ in {بِهِ}, i.e.: we believed in it, and that exalted is the majesty of our Lord, and that he used to … to the end; conjoining to the genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition, with «أنَّ», is not prevented, because of the frequent omission of the preposition with «أنَّ».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (وأنه كان يقول سفيهنا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The noun of kāna is the latent (mustatir) pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause «يقول» is its khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun «على الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شططا»; «شططًا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: an outrageous saying; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: His words «أن لن»: «أن» is the lightened [one], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) stands in place of the two objects of «ظن»; the clause «لن تقول» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; the preposition and its genitive noun «على الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كذبًا», and «كذبًا» is the object of «تقول».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من الإنس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رجال»; the clause «يعوذون» is the khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause «فزادوهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «كان», and «رَهَقا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), i.e.: they thought a thinking like your thinking; «أنْ» is lightened, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); «أن» with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «ظن», and the clause «يبعث» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «وجد» takes one object because it means "we came upon" and "we found"; the clause «مُلئت» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, and «حرسًا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «مقاعد» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the preposition and its genitive noun «للسمع» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نقعد»; the preposition and its genitive noun «منها» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مقاعد»; the conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «كنا»; «من» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); «الآن» is an adverb originally for the present, borrowed for the future; the preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to «يجد».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «لا ندري» is the khabar (predicate) of «أنَّ»; the hamza is interrogative, and it is mostly followed by a verb, though it may be followed by a noun, as in this verse; the clause «أشر أريد» stands in place of the two objects of «درى»; «أم» is a connected (muttaṣila) conjunction; the clause «أراد بهم ربهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أشرٌّ أريد», and this clause is interpreted as a single word, i.e.: is evil intended for them or good?

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: His words «الصالحون»: a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «منا الصالحون» is the khabar (predicate) of «أنَّ»; «دون» is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ, i.e.: and among us are people who are below; the omission of the qualified noun with the partitive «مِنْ» is frequent. The meaning is: and among us are righteous ones below those in righteousness. The clause «ومنَّا قومٌ دون ذلك» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «منَّا الصالحون»; and the clause «كنَّا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun «نا» in his words «مِنَّا».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «أن» is the lightened [one], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the preposition and its genitive noun «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «نعجز»; «هَربًا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, i.e.: fleeing.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The first conditional clause and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) are the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; the clause «فمن يؤمن» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «آمنا», the linking element being implied (muqaddar), i.e.: of us (مِنَّا); the clause «فلا يخاف» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هو" (he), and the nominal clause is the apodosis; «فلا يخاف» [by itself] is not the apodosis, because an apodosis joined with «لا» is free of the fāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: (وأنا منا المسلمون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding maṣdar; the clause «منَّا المسلمون» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; the clause «منا القاسطون» is conjoined to the clause «منَّا المسلمون»; the conditional clause is conjoined to the clause «منَّا المسلمون», the linking element being implied (muqaddar), i.e.: [whoever] of us submitted (أسلم منَّا); «رشدًا» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «مَنْ أسلم»; the preposition and its genitive noun «لجهنم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حطبًا».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «أن» is the lightened [one], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the khabar (predicate) is the clause «لو استقاموا»; «ماء» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: (ومن يعرض عن ذكر ربه يسلكه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «لا» is prohibitive; «مع» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أحدًا».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The conditional clause is the khabar (predicate) of «أنَّ»; the preposition and its genitive noun «عليه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لبدًا»; the clause «يدعوه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «قام».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ضرًا».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the preposition and its genitive noun «من دونه» is attached to «أجد».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: His words «إلا بلاغًا»: a disconnected excepted [noun] (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ); the preposition and its genitive noun «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «بلاغًا»; the conditional clause is resumptive. «خالدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «له», construed according to the meaning of «مَنْ», and therefore plural; «أبدًا» is an adverb of time attached to «خالدين».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), and the conditional clause is resumptive; «من» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أضعف» is the khabar (predicate); the clause stands in place of the two objects of «علم»; «ناصرًا» is tamyīz (specification).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «إن» is negative; «قريب» is the khabar (predicate) of the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ما توعدون», i.e.: the promise is near; the clause «قريب ما توعدون» stands in place of the two objects of «أدري»; «أم» is a connected (muttaṣila) conjunction; the clause «يجعل له ربي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «قريب ما توعدون»; the preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «عالم» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied (muqaddar) «هو», and the clause «فلا يظهر» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause (هو عالم).

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «مَنْ» is a relative noun, a badal (substitute) from {أَحَدًا}; the preposition and its genitive noun «من رسول» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَنْ»; the clause «فإنه يسلك» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ارتضى»; and the preposition and its genitive noun «مِنْ بين» is attached to «يسلك».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليعلم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يَسْلُكُ}; «أن» is lightened, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «قد أبلغوا» is the khabar (predicate); «أن» with what follows it, interpreted as a maṣdar, stands in place of the two objects of «علم»; «لديهم» is an adverb of place attached to the ṣila (relative clause); «عددًا» is tamyīz (specification).

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (أنه استمع): (أن) is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) because it is the object whose agent is not named, i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), of (أوحي). Then what comes after it with the wording (أن) is conjoined to it, so (أن) is in the position of the nominative in all of that. It is also said that (أن) was given fatḥa in the rest of the verses by referring them back to the hāʾ in (آمنا به); that is permissible although it is a genitive pronoun, on the basis of omitting the preposition, because of how often it is omitted with (أن). Conjunction with (آمنا به), in reading (أن) with fatḥa, is more complete in meaning than conjunction with (أنه استمع), because if you conjoined (وأنا ظننا), (وأنا لما سمعنا الهدى), (وأنه كان رجال من الإنس), (وأنا لمسنا) and the like to (أنه استمع), it would not be permissible, since it is not part of what was revealed to them; it is only something they reported about themselves. Kasra in all of this is clearer, and a group of the readers follow it. Fatḥa in that is by construing it according to the meaning of (آمنا به), and there is something novel [Translator's note: «بدع»; perhaps «بعد» "far-fetchedness" is intended] in the meaning, because they did not report that they believed that, when they heard the guidance, they believed in it, nor did they report that they believed that there were men...; Allah only related of them that they said that, reporting it about themselves to their companions. So kasra is more fitting for that.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying (وأنه كان رجال): the hāʾ in (أنه) is the noun of (أن), and it is the implied pronoun of the matter and the account. (رجال) is the noun of (كان) and (يعوذون) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان). (من الإنس) is a naʿt (adjective) of (رجال); that is why it is good for an indefinite noun to be the noun of (كان): when it was qualified it came close to the definite, so it may be the noun of (كان). (كان) with its noun and khabar is the khabar of (أن).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t:
His saying (فوجدناها ملئت): (وجد) takes two objects: the hāʾ is the first and (ملئت) is in the position of the second. You may also make it take one object and make (ملئت) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) with an implied (قد); the first is better. (حرسا) is accusative as a specification (tafsīr), and likewise (شهبا).
His saying (وأنه كان يقول سفيهنا على الله): the hāʾ in (أنه) is for the account, and it is the noun of (أن). In (كان) is its noun, and what comes after it is the khabar (predicate). It is also said that (سفيهنا) is the noun of (كان) and (يقول) is the khabar placed first; but this is far-fetched, because when the verb comes first it governs the noun after it. It is also permissible for (كان) to be redundant (zāʾida).

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying (ولن نعجزه هربا): (هربا) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that stands in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying (عذابا): an object of (يسلكه), meaning "into a punishment". One says (سلكه) and (أسلكه), two dialects with one meaning. It has been read (نسلكه) with ḍamma on the nūn, according to "I made it enter (أسلكته) into such-and-such".

mekki-muskil:18-18.t:
His saying (وأن المساجد لله): (أن) is in the position of the nominative by conjunction with (أنه استمع). It is also said that it is in the position of the genitive with the preposition implied; this is the school of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī. It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative because the preposition is absent; this is the school of a group of grammarians.
His saying (فسيعلمون من أضعف ناصرا): (من) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) because it is interrogative, and (أضعف) is the khabar (predicate). (ناصرا) is accusative as an explanation (bayān), and likewise (عددا). The clause is in the position of the accusative governed by (سيعلمون). If you make (من) mean (الذي), it is in the position of the accusative governed by the verb, and you put (أضعف) and (أقل) in the nominative with an implied (هو), a mubtadaʾ and khabar within the ṣila (relative clause) of (من) when it means (الذي); it has no ṣila when it is interrogative.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying (إلا بلاغا): accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It is also said that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) with an implied verb; on this view (إلا) is separated, (إن) is conditional and (لا) means (لم). The implied form is: "No one will protect me from Allah, and I will not find besides Him a refuge, if I do not convey the messages of my Lord a conveying." (الملتحد) is the refuge.
His saying (ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم): this is a condition, and its answer is the fāʾ. It is general for everyone who disobeys Allah, except what the Qur'an has made clear about forgiving minor sins by avoiding major sins, and about forgiveness for whoever repents and does righteous deeds, and what the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace, made clear about bringing out of the Fire the monotheists among the people of sins.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (قل إن أدري أقريب): (إن) means (ما) [negation]. (قريب) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ما), meaning (الذي), is in the position of the nominative governed by (قريب) and stands in place of the khabar (predicate); or, if you wish, make it the khabar of (قريب). The clause is in the position of the accusative governed by (أدري). The hāʾ is omitted from (توعدون), referring back to (ما); the implied form is "Is the time which you are promised near?" You may also make (ما) with the verb a maṣdar, so it needs no returning pronoun.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t: His saying (إلا من ارتضى من رسول): (من) is in the position of the accusative as an exception from (أحد), because it has the meaning of a group.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying (ليعلم أن قد): the pronoun in (ليعلم) refers back to Allah, exalted be His mention; it is also said to the Prophet, and also said to the polytheists. The pronoun in (أبلغوا) refers back to the prophets; it is also said to the angels who descend with the revelation to the prophets.
His saying (عددا): accusative as an explanation (bayān); had it been a maṣdar (verbal noun) it would have been assimilated [Translator's note: i.e. it would be «عدّا»].

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت), i.e.: O Muhammad.
﴿أُوحي﴾: a past verb whose agent is not named (passive).
﴿إليّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أُوحي﴾.
﴿أنه﴾: أن with what falls within its scope is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); أن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿استمع﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī); and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أن.
﴿نفر﴾: the fāʿil of استمع.
﴿من الجن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿نفر﴾; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أنه استمع﴾ is the nāʾib fāʿil.
﴿فقالوا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿استمع﴾.
﴿إنا﴾: inna is an abrogating particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism.
﴿سمعنا﴾: a past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; and the clause is the khabar of inna.
﴿قرآنا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿عجبا﴾: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿يهدي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the clause is a second attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿قرآنا﴾.
﴿إلى الرشد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يهدي﴾.
﴿فآمنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; آمنا is a past verb and its fāʿil; and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿سمعنا﴾.
﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿آمنّا﴾.
﴿ولن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لن is a particle of negation, subjunctive and future.
﴿نشرك﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by ﴿لن﴾, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "we" (نحن).
﴿بربنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نشرك﴾; and ﴿نا﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿أحدا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿نشرك﴾.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وأنه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the hāʾ is the ism (noun) of anna; anna with what falls within its scope is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded.
﴿تعالى﴾: a past verb.
﴿جدّ﴾: fāʿil (agent), and it is muḍāf.
﴿ربنا﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause ﴿تعالى جد ربنا﴾ is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) with no grammatical position.
﴿ما﴾: negating.
﴿اتخذ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir).
﴿صاحبة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿أن﴾.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is connective (ṣila).
﴿ولدا﴾: conjoined to صاحبة. And the clause ﴿ما اتخذ...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of anna; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أنه...ما اتخذ﴾ is nominative (marfūʿ), conjoined to its like in the first ayah.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وأنه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the hāʾ is the ism (noun) of anna; anna with what falls within its scope is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded.
﴿كان﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb; its ism is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being: "he" (هو); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna. [Translator's note: so in the source («إن»); the particle here is أنّ.]
﴿يقول﴾: an imperfect verb.
﴿سفيهنا﴾: fāʿil (agent), and it is muḍāf, and ﴿نا﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿على الله﴾: على is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقول﴾.
﴿شططا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e.: "an outrageous saying" (قولا شططا); and the clause يقول is the khabar of ﴿كان﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿وأنّا﴾: the wāw conjoins to what preceded; anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿ظننا﴾: ظن is a past verb, one of the verbs of the heart (afʿāl al-qulūb), and نا is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause ظننا is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿أن﴾: lightened from the heavy (form) (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla); its ism is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
﴿لن﴾: a particle of negation, subjunctive and future.
﴿تقول﴾: an imperfect verb; and the clause ﴿لن تقول...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the lightened أن.
﴿الإنس﴾: fāʿil.
﴿والجن﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الإنس.
﴿على الله﴾: على is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تقول﴾.
﴿كذبا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an attribute of the maṣdar, its implied form being: "a false saying" (قولا كذبا).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وأنه﴾: anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun); and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf).
﴿كان﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb.
﴿رجال﴾: the ism of kāna.
﴿من الإنس﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رجال﴾; and the clause كان is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿أن﴾.
﴿يعوذون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is the khabar of kāna.
﴿برجال﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يعوذون﴾.
﴿من الجن﴾: attached to an omitted naʿt of ﴿رجال﴾.
﴿فزادوهم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (زادوا is) a past verb, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is conjoined to ﴿كان رجال﴾.
﴿رهقا﴾: second object.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وأنهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun); and the clause is likewise conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded.
﴿ظنوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna.
﴿كما ظننتم﴾: كما: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as an attribute (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar; and ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), construed with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause ﴿ظننتم﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative ﴿ما﴾.
﴿أن﴾: lightened from the heavy (form) (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla); its ism is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
﴿لن﴾: a particle of negation, subjunctive and future.
﴿يبعث﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by ﴿لن﴾; and the clause ﴿لن يخرج الله...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أن. [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause in this ayah is ﴿لن يبعث الله أحدا﴾.]
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, the fāʿil of يبعث.
﴿أحدا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of ظنوا.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وأنا﴾: the wāw conjoins to what preceded; anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿لمسنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna.
﴿السماء﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فوجدناها﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and وجدناها is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ملئت﴾: a past verb whose agent is not named (passive), its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هي); and the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi. It has also been said: a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿حرسا﴾: tamyīz (specification).
﴿شديدا﴾: a naʿt (adjective).
﴿وشهبا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿حرسا﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وأنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿كنّا﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism; and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna.
﴿نقعد﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "we" (نحن); and the clause is the khabar of ﴿كان﴾.
﴿منها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مقاعد﴾.
﴿مقاعد﴾: an adverb (ẓarf), attached to ﴿نقعد﴾.
﴿للسمع﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an implied element which is an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿مقاعد﴾, i.e.: "seats existing for listening".
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and من is a conditional noun that puts into the jussive (ism sharṭ jāzim), a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يستمع﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
﴿الآن﴾: an adverb of the present, borrowed for the future; it is attached to ﴿يستمع﴾.
﴿يجد﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive, as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿شهابا﴾: the first object of يجد.
﴿رصدا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿شهابا﴾; and the condition clause with its apodosis is the khabar of من.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وأنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿ندري﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna.
﴿أشر﴾: there are two ways of construing it: the nominative by an implied verb, on the pattern of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), the clause ﴿أريد﴾ then being explicative with no grammatical position. The second way: the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause ﴿أريد﴾ then being in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
﴿أُريد﴾: a past verb whose agent is not named (passive), its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being: "it" (هو).
﴿بمن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أُريد﴾.
﴿في الأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿من﴾; and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position.
﴿أم﴾: an equating conjunction (muʿādila).
﴿أراد﴾: a past verb.
﴿بهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أراد﴾.
﴿ربهم﴾: fāʿil (agent); رب is muḍāf, and هم is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿رشدا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿وأنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is the ism (noun) of anna.
﴿منا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿الصالحون﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; and the clause is the khabar of anna.
﴿ومنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar.
﴿دون﴾: an adverb of place, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of an implied ﴿قوم﴾, and it is muḍāf.
﴿ذلك﴾: the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded.
﴿كنا﴾: ﴿كان﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism.
﴿طرائق﴾: the khabar of kāna.
﴿قددا﴾: a naʿt, accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وأنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is the ism (noun) of anna; and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded.
﴿ظننا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿أن﴾: lightened from the heavy (form) (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla); its ism is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
﴿لن﴾: a particle of negation, subjunctive and future.
﴿نعجز﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "we" (نحن); and the clause ﴿لن نعجز الله...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أن; and أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of ظن.
﴿في الأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ولن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لن is a particle of negation, subjunctive and future.
﴿نعجزه﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive, with a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is conjoined to ﴿لن نعجز الله﴾.
﴿هربا﴾: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, its implied form being: "we will never escape Him, fleeing to the sky and going deep into it".

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿وأنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the clause likewise being conjoined (maʿṭūf); anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿لما﴾: linking (rābiṭa), or temporal ("when", ḥīniyya).
﴿سمعنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿الهدى﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied fatḥa because pronouncing it is impossible.
﴿آمنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. And the condition clause with its apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of anna.
﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿آمنّا﴾.
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and من is a conditional noun that puts into the jussive (ism sharṭ jāzim), a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يؤمن﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), and its fāʿil is "he" (هو).
﴿بربه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يؤمن﴾.
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is linking, and لا is negating.
﴿يخاف﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil is "he" (هو); the clause لا يخاف is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: "then he does not fear"; and the nominal clause joined to the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the condition clause with its apodosis is the khabar of من.
﴿بخسا﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ولا رهقا﴾: conjoined to ﴿بخسا﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وأنا﴾: likewise conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded; anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿منّا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿المسلمون﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; and the clause is the khabar of ﴿أنّ﴾.
﴿ومنّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to a fronted khabar.
﴿القاسطون﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is conjoined to ﴿منّا المسلمون﴾.
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and من is a conditional noun that puts into the jussive (ism sharṭ jāzim), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿أسلم﴾: a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
﴿فأولئك﴾: the fāʾ is linking, and أولئك is mubtadaʾ.
﴿تحروا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is the khabar.
﴿رشدا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿وأما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and أما is a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl).
﴿القاسطون﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw.
﴿فكانوا﴾: the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; كانوا is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its ism (noun); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿القاسطون﴾.
﴿لجهنم﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿حطبا﴾ and was put before it.
﴿حطبا﴾: the khabar of kāna.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وألو﴾: likewise conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أنه استمع; أن is lightened from the heavy (form) (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its ism being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); and لو is conditional. [Translator's note: the quoted word is so in the source; the text of the ayah is ﴿وأن لو﴾ (written وألّو in the muṣḥaf).]
﴿استقاموا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and the clause ﴿لو استقاموا...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿أن﴾.
﴿على الطريقة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿استقاموا﴾.
﴿لأسقيناهم﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; أسقيناهم is a verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ماء is the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿غدقا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ماء﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿لنفتنهم﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl), and نفتنهم is an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause, the fāʿil (agent) being "we" (نحن), with a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أسقيناهم﴾.
﴿فيه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نفتنهم﴾.
﴿ومن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يعرض﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm).
﴿عن ذكر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يعرض﴾; and ذكر is muḍāf.
﴿ربه﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿يسلكه﴾: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi.
﴿عذابا﴾: accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the original being: "We make him enter into a punishment" (نسلكه في عذاب). [Translator's note: so in the source, with the first-person نسلكه; the ayah reads ﴿يسلكه﴾ (نسلكه is a variant reading).]
﴿صعدا﴾: a naʿt (adjective), accusative.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿وأن﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿أنه استمع﴾; and anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿المساجد﴾: the ism (noun) of anna.
﴿لله﴾: the lām is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of anna.
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لا is prohibitive (nāhiya).
﴿تدعوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn.
﴿مع﴾: an adverb, attached to ﴿تدعوا﴾, and it is muḍāf.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿أحدا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وأنه﴾: likewise conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿أنه استمع﴾; anna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿لما﴾: linking (rābiṭa), or a temporal adverb ("when") containing the meaning of condition.
﴿قام﴾: a past verb.
﴿عبد﴾: fāʿil (agent), and it is muḍāf.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿يدعوه﴾: an imperfect verb, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being: "he" (هو), and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause يدعوه is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: "calling (upon Him)".
﴿كادوا﴾: كاد is a past verb, one of the verbs of approximation (afʿāl al-muqāraba), and the wāw is its ism; the clause كادوا has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. And لما with its condition and its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of anna.
﴿يكونون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the ism of يكون; and the clause is the khabar of ﴿كادوا﴾.
﴿عليه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl.
﴿لبدا﴾: the khabar of يكون, accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿قل﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; قل is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), referring to the Prophet, upon him be peace.
﴿إنما﴾: a restraining and restrained (particle) (kāffa wa-makfūfa).
﴿أدعو﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), with a latent fāʿil, its implied form being: "I" (أنا).
﴿ربي﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied fatḥa because of the (vowel) agreement (with the yāʾ); رب is muḍāf, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negating.
﴿أشرك﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "I" (أنا).
﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أشرك﴾.
﴿أحدا﴾: mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿قل﴾: likewise a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; قل is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), referring to the Prophet, upon him be peace.
﴿إني﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿لا أملك﴾: لا is negating, and أملك is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "I" (أنا); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ضرّا﴾.
﴿ضرّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ولا رشدا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿ضرا﴾: لا is negating, and رشدا is a conjoined noun; and the clause ﴿إني لا أملك﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿قل﴾: likewise a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; قل is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), referring to the Prophet, upon him be peace.
﴿إني﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿لن﴾: a particle of negation, subjunctive and future.
﴿يجيرني﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) [Translator's note: so in the source; after لن the verb is in fact subjunctive (manṣūb)]; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause لن يجيرني is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿من الله﴾: من is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يجيرني﴾.
﴿أحد﴾: the fāʿil of يجيرني.
﴿ولن﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿لن يجيرني﴾; and لن is a particle of negation, subjunctive and future.
﴿أجد﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative [Translator's note: so in the source; after لن it is subjunctive], its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "I" (أنا).
﴿من دونه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿أجد﴾; دون is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ملتحدا﴾: the first object of ﴿أجد﴾.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿بلاغا﴾: a badal (substitute) of ﴿ملتحدا﴾, or an excepted (mustathnā), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿من الله﴾: من is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿بلاغا﴾.
﴿ورسالاته﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and رسالات is a conjoined (maʿṭūf) noun; it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ومن﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يعص﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ورسوله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and رسوله is a conjoined noun; it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿فإن﴾: the fāʾ binds the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿نار﴾: the postponed ism (noun) of inna, and it is muḍāf.
﴿جهنم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. And the clause ﴿ومن يعص الله...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿خالدين﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ﴿له﴾; the governing word of this ḥāl is the omitted (notion of) "being established" (al-istiqrār).
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خالدين﴾.
﴿أبدا﴾: an adverb of time, accusative, likewise attached to ﴿خالدين﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿حتى﴾: a particle of commencement (ḥarf ibtidāʾ).
﴿إذا﴾: a future adverb containing the meaning of condition.
﴿رأوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, because pronouncing it is impossible, on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿يوعدون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil [Translator's note: so in the source; since the verb is passive, the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]; and the clause ﴿يوعدون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿فسيعلمون﴾: the fāʾ is linking, in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the sīn is a particle of the future; يعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, mafʿūl bihi.
﴿أضعف﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿ناصرا﴾: tamyīz (specification).
﴿وأقل﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿أضعف﴾.
﴿عددا﴾: tamyīz.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿قل﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿إن﴾: negating.
﴿أدري﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "I" (أنا).
﴿أقريب﴾: the hamza is interrogative, and قريب is a fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿ما﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿توعدون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; and the interpreted maṣdar from the maṣdar-forming ﴿ما﴾ and ﴿توعدون﴾ is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause ﴿توعدون﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdar-forming ﴿ما﴾. Or ﴿ما﴾ may be a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, the clause ﴿توعدون﴾ being the ṣila of the relative noun with no grammatical position.
﴿أم﴾: connected (muttaṣila).
﴿يجعل﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ربي﴾: fāʿil, nominative, the sign of its nominative being an implied ḍamma because of the (vowel) agreement (with the yāʾ); it is muḍāf, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿أمدا﴾: the first object of يجعل; and the clause, suspended (muʿallaqa) by the interrogative, is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ﴿أدري﴾.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿عالم﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: "He is the Knower", or a badal (substitute) of ربي; and it is muḍāf.
﴿الغيب﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, to make the non-disclosure follow upon His being alone in knowledge of the unseen absolutely; and لا is negating.
﴿يظهر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿على غيبه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يظهر﴾; غيب is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أحدا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of أحد.
﴿ارتضى﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿فإنه﴾: the fāʾ is causal, inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿من بين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسلك﴾; and بين is muḍāf.
﴿يديه﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); يدي is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ومن خلفه﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿من بين يديه﴾; خلف is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿رصدا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); and the clause يسلك is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿إنه﴾, i.e.: "He sends (lit. makes go) guarding angels".

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿ليعلم﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl), and يعلم is an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسلك﴾, or to an omitted element.
﴿أن﴾: lightened from the heavy (form) (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla); its ism is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn).
﴿قد﴾: a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq).
﴿أبلغوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw of the plural; and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿رسالات﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the kasra in place of the fatḥa; and it is muḍāf.
﴿ربهم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); رب is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause ﴿قد أبلغوا...﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أن.
﴿وأحاط﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and أحاط is a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿بما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ما: a relative noun in the position of the genitive; both are attached to ﴿أحاط﴾.
﴿لديهم﴾: لدى: an adverb, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. لدى is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وأحصى﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and أحصى is a past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿كل﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative; and it is muḍāf.
﴿شيء﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
﴿عددا﴾: tamyīz (specification) converted from the object, i.e.: "He has counted the number of everything". It has also been said: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿كل شيء﴾, i.e.: "being counted"; or standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it has the meaning of "counting" (إحصاء).

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: Because they considered that something enormous; and al-ẓann (supposition) here means doubt.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: The noun of kāna (kāna and its sisters) and its khabar (predicate): يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجالٍ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَزادُوهُمْ رَهَقاً — (رَهَقاً) is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّوا كَما ظَنَنْتُمْ: if you read «أنّ» with fatḥa, you likewise construe it according to the sense, i.e. "we learned that they thought as you thought". أَنْ لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ أَحَداً: «أن» and what follows it are in the position of the two objects of (ظننتم) if you make it the governing verb; and if you make the first verb govern, you intend it [i.e. «أن» and its clause] as placed earlier.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: If you make وجدنا take two objects, then (فملئت) is in the position of the second object; and if you make it take one object, you imply «قد». Abū Jaʿfar said: the first is preferable. And (شهب) [is the plural] for many, while for few [the plural is] أشهبة.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: وَأَنَّا كُنَّا نَقْعُدُ مِنْها مَقاعِدَ لِلسَّمْعِ: (مَقاعِدَ) is a diptote (not inflected for tanwīn) because it has no counterpart among singular forms, and it is the ultimate plural pattern. فَمَنْ يَسْتَمِعِ الْآنَ يَجِدْ لَهُ شِهاباً رَصَداً: a condition and its requital (sharṭ wa-mujāzāh).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: The best of what has been said about it is that the meaning is: we do not know whether Allah intended evil for those on earth when He prevented us from listening [to the news] from heaven, or whether their Lord intended for them to send them a messenger who would guide them aright. This is the view of Ibn Zayd. This was one of the signs of his prophethood ﷺ: that the devils were dealt with severely in their listening from heaven and were pelted with shooting stars.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Since the nūn of «من» is vowelless, you did without adding another nūn [in مِنَّا]; but when you say منّي, the noun is the yāʾ, and you add the nūn so that the nūn of «من» is not given kasra. كُنَّا طَرائِقَ قِدَداً: the singular is طريقة; one says طريق and طريقة. "So-and-so follows the طريقة (way) of so-and-so"; and "so-and-so is the طريقة of the people", i.e. their chief; and the people [as a whole] are also called طريقة, and if you wish you put it in the plural.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا أَنْ لَنْ نُعْجِزَ اللَّهَ فِي الْأَرْضِ: al-ẓann here means certainty. وَلَنْ نُعْجِزَهُ هَرَباً: (هَرَباً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعْنَا الْهُدى آمَنَّا بِهِ: [the pronoun in بِهِ] treats الْهُدى as masculine, and that is the most eloquent usage; it is sometimes treated as feminine. فَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِرَبِّهِ فَلا يَخافُ بَخْساً وَلا رَهَقاً: the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash is فَلا يَخافُ «[Translator's note: the variant form of the verb appears to have dropped out of the source text here; the reading meant is presumably the jussive فَلا يَخَفْ.]» as a prohibition.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: وَأَنَّا مِنَّا الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا الْقاسِطُونَ: قسط means "to act unjustly"; this is the root, and then an alif is added to it, so one says أقسط when one removes injustice (القسوط), i.e. acts justly.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
The reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash is وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا with ḍamma on the wāw, because of the meeting of two vowelless letters and because the ḍamma resembles the wāw; except that Sībawayh allows only kasra on an original wāw, to distinguish it from the added one. لَأَسْقَيْناهُمْ ماءً غَدَقاً: Abū ʿUbayda reported that سقيته and أسقيته are [two] dialectal forms; al-Aṣmaʿī, however, said: سقيته [means] "[I gave him to drink] to his mouth", and أسقيته [means] "I provided him with a supply of drink". Abū Jaʿfar said: what al-Aṣmaʿī said is the most eloquent usage, and to it belongs لأسقيناهم, i.e. "We would have kept that continually available for them". However, Abū ʿUbayda recited [a verse] of Labīd — whose eloquence is not disputed: [al-Wāfir] 500-
سقى قومي بني مجد وأسقى ... نميرا والقبائل من هلال
(He gave drink to my people, the Banū Majd, and gave drink to Numayr and the tribes of Hilāl.)
Al-Aṣmaʿī was asked about this verse and said: in my view it is contrived, not natural; a [natural poet] does not bring two dialectal forms in one verse.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ: Abū Zayd and Abū ʿUbayda reported فتنته and أفتنته. Abū Zayd said: أفتنته is the dialect of Banū Tamīm. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: فتنه, يفتنه, so he is فاتن and فتّان; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ما أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ بِفاتِنِينَ [al-Ṣāffāt: 162]. He said: one does not say أفتنه — and he rejected this form and did not recognise it. So they recited to him: [al-Ṭawīl] 501-
لئن فتنتني لهي بالأمس أفتنت ... سعيدا فأمسى قد قلا كلّ مسلم
(If she has captivated me, well, yesterday she captivated Saʿīd, so that he came to loathe every Muslim.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is old poetry; however, al-Aṣmaʿī said: no matter — we have heard this from an effeminate man, so no attention is paid to it, even if it was said long ago. Abū Jaʿfar said: the eminent authorities on the language, whose word is relied upon for truthfulness, have reported فتنه and أفتنه; but Sībawayh distinguished between them, holding that the transitive one is أفتن, and that the meaning of فتنه is "he put fitna into him", just as you say كحّله ("he put kohl on him"). وَمَنْ يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ عَذاباً صَعَداً: Muslim ibn Jundab read نَسْلُكُهُ with ḍamma on the nūn. Abū Jaʿfar said: سلكه and أسلكه are two dialectal forms according to many of the authorities on the language, while al-Aṣmaʿī said: سلكه, without alif. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ما سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ [al-Muddaththir: 42], and as the poet said:
[al-Basīṭ] 502-
أمّا سلكت سبيلا كنت سالكها ... فاذهب فلا يبعدنك الله منتشر ]
(Since you have taken a path you were bound to take, go then — may Allah not keep you far, O Muntashir.)
And سلك / سلكته are like رجع / رجعته; and أسلكته is a well-known dialectal form. Abū ʿUbayda and others recited [the verse] of ʿAbd Manāf ibn Ribʿ: [al-Basīṭ] 503-
حتّى إذا أسلكوهم في قتائدة ... شلّا كما تطرد الجمّالة الشّردا
(Until, when they had driven them into [the pass of] Qatāʾida, a driving such as camel-herders drive the strays.)
Al-Aṣmaʿī did not impugn this verse, except that he said: أسلكه means "he made him take [the path]". Abū ʿUbayda claimed that the apodosis (jawāb) [of إذا] is omitted, and he was contradicted on this; it has been said: the apodosis is شلّوا ("they drove"), and شلّا stands in its place.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ: «أنّ» is in the position of naṣb (accusative), in the sense of "and because"; and according to the view of some, it is in the position of rafʿ (nominative), conjoined to قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ. فَلا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَداً: a prohibition addressed to a group, and the nūn has been dropped from it for the jussive (jazm).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: «لبدا» means "helpers". Mujāhid said [about] وَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا قامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يَدْعُوهُ كادُوا يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً (19): لبدا means "groups"; and مالا لبدا [Q 90:6] means "much [wealth]". Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a clear view; and even if this has been read لِبَداً, it is far-fetched, and the meaning is "the group", not "abundance" as Mujāhid said «[Translator's note: the source has «الأعلى الكثرة», apparently «لا على الكثرة», "not abundance"; translated accordingly.]». It is from تلبّد الشيء على الشيء, when a thing gathers upon a thing and sticks to it; and "he has a لبدة", i.e. hair and the like, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 504-
لدى أسد شاكي السّلاح مقاذف ... له لبد أظفاره لم تقلّم
(With a lion, bristling with weapons, hurling [himself] into battle, with a thick mane, whose claws have not been clipped.)

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: And it is read قُلْ إِنَّما أَدْعُوا رَبِّي; and the reading «[Translator's note: i.e. the other reading, قالَ.]» is said to be connected [to what precedes] and is also said to be cut off [from it]; both meanings are sound, i.e. "Say to them" — so he said: "I only call upon my Lord". وَلا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ أَحَداً is conjoined (nasaq), and it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: I.e. I have no power to harm you in your religion or your worldly life, except that I guide you كرها «[Translator's note: so in the source; the word is unclear here and is perhaps a corruption.]», i.e. except that I convey [the message] to you. There is another view on it: it is accusative by an implied verb, and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "Say: none can protect me from Allah except that I convey His message"; so «أن» is separate from لا «[Translator's note: i.e. إِلَّا is analysed as إنْ + لا.]». And the meaning is: "except as a conveying of what has come to me from Allah and His messages". وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نارَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً: a condition and its requital; and in the speech of the Arabs it is general for everyone who disobeys Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except those excepted by a verse of the Qur'an, or by explicit authority (tawqīf) from the Messenger ﷺ, or by consensus of the Muslims. What has come as excepted from it is: whoever repents and believes, and whoever commits a minor sin and avoids the major sins; the rest of that is included in the verse, except what is soundly reported from the Prophet about the monotheists coming out of the Fire.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: لَنْ makes the verb future only. وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداً: i.e. a refuge to which I resort and turn. And the لحد (niche) in the grave is from this, because it inclines to one side of it, and the dead person is inclined into it.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: إِلَّا بَلاغاً مِنَ اللَّهِ: accusative as an exception (istithnāʾ), and the meaning in it when it is an exception [is as given above].

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) and it is not inflected, because it resembles particles in its shifting [reference] and because it carries the meaning of requital (mujāzāh); and its apodosis is فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَضْعَفُ ناصِراً. «من» is in the position of rafʿ (nominative) because it is interrogative, and what precedes an interrogative does not govern it — this is the [preferred] way. If you make it mean "who" (الذي), it is in the position of naṣb (accusative), and you imply a mubtadaʾ (subject), with أَضْعَفُ as its khabar (predicate). وَأَقَلُّ is conjoined to it. عَدَداً is accusative as clarification (bayān) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)].

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: أَدْرِي is in the position of rafʿ (nominative), the ḍamma having been dropped from it; whoever puts it in the accusative has committed a solecism that is not permissible. أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ is a naʿt (adjective). فَلا يُظْهِرُ عَلى غَيْبِهِ أَحَداً.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضى مِنْ رَسُولٍ: in the position of naṣb (accusative) as an exception from أحد, because أحد has the meaning of a group. فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً: in the meaning of a group, i.e. possessors of watchfulness from among the angels, who guard him and guard what descends of the revelation, so that it is neither altered nor stolen by listening.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: لِيَعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ أَبْلَغُوا رِسالاتِ رَبِّهِمْ: we have mentioned it already. وَأَحاطَ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ: a conjoining of a clause [to a clause], because what precedes it is future while this is past; and likewise وَأَحْصى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عَدَداً.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Juwayya ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Asadī read «قل أحي إليّ» («قل أُوحِيَ إليّ»).
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is according to the dialect of those who say «وحى يحي». Al-ʿAjjāj said: [al-Rajaz] 498- وحى لها القرار فاستقرّت
(He inspired it [the earth] to be still, and it became still.)
The origin is «وُحِيَ إليّ», and a hamza was substituted for the wāw, as in أُقِّتَتْ. «أنه» is in the position of the nominative as the noun of the verb whose agent is not named [i.e. deputy agent, nāʾib fāʿil]. «النفر» is three or more. فَقالُوا إِنَّا سَمِعْنا قُرْآناً عَجَباً: «إن» takes kasra because it comes after «قول» (saying), so it begins a new sentence. The meaning of «عَجَب» (wonderful) in the language, according to what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd mentioned, is a thing that is rare and whose like is hardly ever found.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
«لن» indicates the future; its origin, according to al-Khalīl,
is «لا أن». Abū ʿUbayda claimed that the jussive is sometimes formed with it.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَأَنَّهُ تَعالى جَدُّ رَبِّنا: this is the reading of the Medinans [i.e. «وإنه», with kasra] [Translator's note: the vowelled text shows «وَأَنَّهُ» with fatḥa; the Medinan reading described is with kasra]
throughout the sūra, except in قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ, in وَأَنَّ الْمَساجِدَ لِلَّهِ [verse: 18] and in وأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ [verse: 16]. Some of the lexicographers claimed that the reading of the Medinans is the only permissible one, and they found fault with whoever read with fatḥa, because he imagined that it is conjoined to أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ. Abū Jaʿfar said: that is an error, because it has been read with fatḥa by those whose reading constitutes a proof. Al-Aʿmash reported from Ibrāhīm, [from] ʿAlqama [Translator's note: the text reads «إبراهيم بن علقمة»; the chain is presumably Ibrāhīm from ʿAlqama], that he read "wa-anna" throughout the sūra. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read with fatḥa throughout the sūra up to His saying قُلْ إِنَّما أَدْعُوا رَبِّي [al-Wāqiʿa: 20] [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse is al-Jinn: 20]; and when this became problematic for him, he turned to the reading of the people of Medina, because it is clear and plain. The explanation of the fatḥa is that it is conjoined according to the meaning; the implied form is "so we believed in it, and we believed that — exalted is the majesty of our Lord", so it is in the position of the accusative. The best thing reported on the meaning of «جَدُّ ربنا» is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās: it is [His] self-sufficiency, greatness and exaltedness. The root sense of «الجَدّ» in the language is elevation; from that comes «الجَدّ», the father's father; and from it «الجَدّ», fortune, which in the Persian language is «بخت». It is said:
the jinn intended this, and they meant elevation and fortune, i.e. our Lord is exalted above being associated with the weakness found in His creatures, such as taking a wife, seeking a child, and desire. This is indicated by what comes after it: مَا اتَّخَذَ صاحِبَةً وَلا وَلَداً. Some of the jurists claimed that it is disliked to say «وتعالى جدُّك» (and exalted is Your majesty), arguing that this is a report of what the jinn said. That is an error, because it is soundly reported from the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah did not blame the jinn for this statement. It is reported from ʿIkrima: «وأنه تعالى جدّا ربّنا» («جَدّا»).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
«السَّفَه» (foolishness) is thinness of forbearance; «ثوبٌ سفيهٌ» means a thin garment. "Anna" is also given fatḥa here, construed according to the meaning, i.e. "we affirmed and testified". «الشطط» is remoteness, as the poet said: [al-Kāmil] 499- شطّت مزار العاشقين فأصبحت
(She became remote from the lovers' visiting place, and became …)

safi-cedvel:1-19.t:
* I'rab:
(إليّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحي), and (الهاء) in (أنّه) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the noun of أنّ; (من الجنّ) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (نفر) ...
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «أوحي ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «استمع نفر ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه استمع ...) is in the position of a nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb أوحي.
The clause «قالوا ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause استمع. The clause «إنّا سمعنا ...» is in the position of an accusative, object of the saying.
The clause «سمعنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
2- (إلى الرشد) attached to (يهدي), (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause; (به) attached to (آمنّا), (الواو) conjunction; (بربّنا) attached to (نشرك).
The clause «يهدى ...» is in the position of an accusative, naʿt of (قرآنا) [Note: Or in the position of an accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial) of (قرآنا), which is qualified by (عجبا).]. The clause «آمنّا ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause سمعنا.
The clause «لن نشرك ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause آمنّا.
3- (الواو) conjunction; (ما) negative; (صاحبة) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the first object being implied (muqaddar), i.e. a woman ...; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation; (ولدا) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to صاحبة [Note: In the speech there is something implied, i.e. "nor anyone as a child".] ...
The clause «تعالى جدّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication [Note: The clause may be the khabar of (أنّ), and the clause after it a ḥāl of ربّنا.].
The clause «ما اتّخذ ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (أنّ). The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه ... ما اتّخذ) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the position of the pronoun in (به), i.e. "we believed in it" [Note: In these verses (أنّ) comes with the hamza vowelled with fatḥa ... so the interpreted maṣdar in them is conjoined to the position of the pronoun in (به), despite the preposition not being repeated; but the omission is regular in this construction beginning with (أنّ).].
4- (الواو) conjunction; (أنّه كان ...) like أنّه استمع, and the noun of (كان) is the pronoun of the matter, omitted [Note: Or an obligatorily latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to the following سفيه, because the verb يقول contends with it for it (tanāzuʿ).], (على الله) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of يقول, i.e. "the fool says, lying against Allah"; (شططا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), being its adjective, i.e. an outrageous saying [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl bihi.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه كان ...) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه ... ما اتّخذ). The clause «كان يقول ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the third (أنّ).
The clause «يقول سفيهنا ...» is in the position of an accusative, khabar of كان ...
5- (الواو) conjunction; (أن) lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its noun being the pronoun of the matter, omitted; (على الله) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of تقول; (كذبا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being its adjective, i.e. a lying saying.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا ظنّنا) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar أنّه كان ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن تقول) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّنا.
The clause «ظننا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the fourth (أنّ).
The clause «لن تقول الإنس ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the lightened (أن).
6- (الواو) conjunction; (أنّه كان ...) like the previous; (من الإنس) attached to a naʿt of (رجال); (برجال) attached to (يعوذون), (من الجنّ) attached to a naʿt of the second (رجال); (الفاء) conjunction; (رهقا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه كان ...) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «كان رجال ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (أنّ).
The clause «يعوذون ...» is in the position of an accusative, khabar of كان.
The clause «زادوهم ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause كان رجال.
7- (الواو) conjunction; (أنّهم ظنّوا) like أنّا ظنّنا; (ما) maṣdar particle; (أن لن يبعث ...) like أن لن تقول ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم ظنّوا) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّه كان..)
The interpreted maṣdar (ما ظننتم) is in the position of a genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "a supposing like your supposing".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن يبعث) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّوا — or of ظننتم — [Note: The other two objects of supposing are omitted, indicated by the maṣdar standing in their place with the other verb of supposing.].
The clause «ظنّوا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «ظننتم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «لن يبعث الله ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the lightened (أن).
8- (الواو) conjunction; (الفاء) likewise; (حرسا) tamyīz (specification), accusative [Note: Or it is a mafʿūl bihi, according to those who make the verb ملأ transitive to two objects.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا لمسنا..) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «لمسنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (أنّ).
The clause «وجدناها ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لمسنا.
The clause «ملئت ...» is in the position of an accusative, second mafʿūl bihi of (وجدناها).
9- (الواو) conjunction; (منها) attached to a ḥāl of مقاعد [Translator's note: the source reads «بحب», evidently a misprint for «بحال».] [Note: Or attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb نقعد, by making it include the meaning of نتّخذ.], (مقاعد) mafʿūl muṭlaq [Note: For it is the plural of the mīmī maṣdar مقعد ... Or it is a mafʿūl bihi of the verb نقعد, by the inclusion of meaning mentioned above, and مقاعد is the plural of the noun of place مقعد.], accusative, i.e. sittings for listening; (للسمع) attached to (نقعد) [Note: Or attached to a naʿt of مقاعد.], i.e. for the sake of listening; (الفاء) resumptive; (من) jussivising conditional noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (يستمع) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents; (الآن) adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative, attached to (يستمع), (له) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّا كنّا..) is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.
The clause «كنّا نقعد ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of أنّ.
The clause «نقعد ...» is in the position of an accusative, khabar of كنّا.
The clause «من يستمع ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يستمع ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of condition and answer together.].
The clause «يجد ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the condition, not joined with the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «جد ربنا» there is a metaphor from الجدّ meaning power and fortune, because kings and the rich are the fortunate (majdūdūn). The meaning: He is described as exalted above having a consort or a child because of His majesty, or because of His authority and dominion, or because of His self-sufficiency.
Metonymic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وأنا لمسنا السماء».
I.e. we sought to reach it to listen to the speech of its inhabitants, or we sought its news. As for اللمس, it has been said: it is borrowed from المسّ (touching) for seeking, like الجسّ (feeling). One says لمسه, التمسه and تلمسه, like طلبه, اطلبه and تطلبه. What is apparent is that the metaphor is lexical, because it is a majāz mursal, being used for what its meaning entails.

* Benefits:
- Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ see the jinn?
The narrators differed as to whether the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the jinn. Ibn Masʿūd affirmed it, in what Muslim narrated from him in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and his ḥadīth has preceded in Sūrat al-Aḥqāf, at the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وإذ صرفنا إليك نفرا من الجن». Ibn ʿAbbās denied it, in what al-Bukhārī and Muslim narrated from him. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not recite to the jinn, nor did he see them.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with a group of his Companions, heading for the market of ʿUkāẓ. The devils had been barred from the news of heaven, and shooting stars had been sent against them. So the devils returned to their people, who said: What is the matter with you? It was said: We have been barred from the news of heaven, and shooting stars have been sent against us. They said:
